diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/tests/wave11_qdiag.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/tests/wave11_qdiag.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..4376e8463f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/tests/wave11_qdiag.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,25 @@
+use snapback4_lang::compile;
+fn checked(source: &str) -> snapback4_lang::Bound { compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]) }
+const REFS: &str = "table parents:\n  read <- allow\ntable kids:\n  parent: parents ? on delete keep\n  read <- allow\n  insert <- allow\n";
+#[test]
+fn optional_reference_checks_join_the_null_edge() {
+    for condition in ["parent != null", "not (parent = null)", "null != parent"] {
+        let b = checked(&format!("{REFS}mutation add(parent: parents ?):\n  if {condition}:\n    row = parents[parent] ! else NOT_FOUND\n  insert kids {{ parent }}\n"));
+        assert!(b.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
+        assert!(!b.notes.iter().any(|n| n.code == "N_REFERENCE_UNCHECKED"), "{:?}", b.notes);
+    }
+    for body in ["  if parent != null:\n    unused = true\n", "  if parent != null and skip:\n    row = parents[parent] ! else NOT_FOUND\n"] {
+        let b = checked(&format!("{REFS}mutation add(parent: parents ?, other: parents ?, skip: bool):\n{body}  insert kids {{ parent }}\n"));
+        assert!(b.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
+        assert!(b.notes.iter().any(|n| n.code == "N_REFERENCE_UNCHECKED"), "{:?}", b.notes);
+    }
+}
+#[test]
+fn syntax_repairs_name_the_actual_form() {
+    let b = checked("mutation add(body: text <=20 = 'hi'):\n  return body\n");
+    assert!(b.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.rewrite.contains("body ?? 'hi'") && d.rewrite.contains("text <=20 ?")), "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
+    let b = checked("mutation add(a: bool, b: bool):\n  require (a or\n    b)\n  else NOPE\n  return true\n");
+    assert!(b.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.rewrite.contains("closing line") && d.rewrite.contains("else NOPE")), "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
+    let b = checked("table parents:\n  public\ntable kids:\n  parent: parents on delete keep ?\n");
+    assert!(b.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.rewrite == "parent: parents ? on delete keep"), "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
+}

2598:**2026-09-17 — lane MQ implementation.** A binder-proven, cursor-free query that is not declared `held` and returns a record of independent fields, each holding at most one read, with no reading `require`, can compose retained and authoritative reads. A found point read of a delivered left row counts as retained. Composition is entered only when at least one field routes to the server and at least one is retained. Every field that would stay local as its own query comes from a second local observation, and only the server-routed fields come from the original query's one server reply. The result's `complete` is the conjunction of the server word and every locally kept field's word; it reports `fresh: false`, no `since`, and no continuation. Composition is never entered while a predictable write is unobserved; the whole local answer stands until it settles. Offline or on request failure, the whole local answer stands. The server and the wire are unchanged.

- **2026-09-12 — `sync` forms (lead).** `sync public`, `sync to .column`,
  `sync to target[.prefix]`, each with an optional `last N by index`
  horizon; the read rule must carry the matching disjunct; a `maintain`
  grouped by the audience inherits it. LLP 2000.000 §14's questions 1 and 2
  are thereby answered: explicit, count horizon optional per table.
- **2026-09-12 — operation names (lead).** Operations in `schema.q` are bare
  (`api.thread`); operations in `snapback/<module>.q` are `<module>.<name>`
  (`api.feed.home`). Generated types are built into
  `snapback/generated/api.ts` by `check` and `dev`, never committed.

- **2026-09-12 — delivery is bound to the rule's probe (lead, after the
  partition review).** `sync to target[.prefix]` is sound only when the
  table's read rule is exactly `exists target[.prefix, viewer]` (a second
  disjunct or a conjunct is refused with the rewrite) and the audience
  index is unique; the partition log delivers by that probe's index and
  never by a mapping reconstructed from column names or types; principal
  partitions are tagged so no principal's name collides with `public`; a

  source's. Horizons bound acquisition, not holdings: a device holds what
  was delivered, and a local read past the horizon says `complete: false`.

  A notified worker remains counted as idle until it reacquires the dispatch
  mutex. The pool must subtract already queued connections before assigning

  approved a minimal vendored tiny_http 0.12.0 fix, with a deterministic

### 18.5 A guess costs a command, not a loop; Trending is on the card

The mechanical set (§5.5, §8) grows by the loops the 0.2.9 lane paid: the
index a read needs (`E_QUARRY_UNKNOWN` naming a `by` line, inserted into the
table's index block in whichever file declares the table); `once` written
on an argument (dropped; the modifier belongs to the column); a field
repeated in a `*` shape (dropped); the parentheses an operation with no
arguments needs (inserted). A mechanical diagnostic prints `check --fix
applies it` after its rewrite, so the command is discovered where the loop
would have been. The feeds card gains the Trending recipe of §5.3 (the
trailing day sought up to the ceiling, sorted, sliced, `complete: false`
past it) beside the maintained ranking. A helper parameter typed by a
table: where helpers are inlined per call and the argument is a row, the
parameter binds as the row; otherwise the diagnostic on a field access names
the point lookup and the shape parameter and no form is added — the lane
reports which.

Built (lane CU5): helpers are inlined per call, so a row passed to a
table-typed parameter binds as the row, and a reference keeps its meaning.

**2026-09-14 — built by lane W5.** The pinned-prefix verdict charges the reservation's static probe count once on either outcome, independent of short-circuit answers; the common attempt and verdict-before-candidate order remain. The shared helper proves all seven meters and complete observations equal for the eight denied pairs and eight true-verdict controls, on both device stores; two-probe rules charge 2 with room and reach 8193 after the 8191-probe prelude, refusing both worlds with `E_BOUND`.

### 20.2 The CLI and client stop inviting mistakes (S02, S03, S22, S28, S32)

- **Assets:** the README's React asset example narrows `status` and renders
  the image, and typechecks.
- **Sign-out:** the `Client` type a builder holds exposes sign-out, or the
  README names the type that does.
- **init:** `init --online`/`--expo` merges into an existing `package.json`
  instead of refusing it.
- **Replayed writes:** a replayed write's result is typed as absent,
  following `issues/20260914-snapback4-write-result-type-omits-replay-state.md`.
- **Replay flags:** `dev --replay` suppresses new effects and holds schedule
  admission without app code (W5a, 2026-09-15; calibration G2). Emission keeps
  its evaluation and meter; a successful mutation or job chunk increments a
  durable suppression count in the same transaction instead of storing an
  effect payload. Refusals and duplicate mutations add no count. `doctor`
  reports `suppressed`; restarting with or without replay never delivers
  these effects. The dev store retains the policy for local `run` until the
  next host start, which sets it from its flags; a normal start clears the
  policy and keeps the count. Replay skips held schedule periods on release
  and already queued jobs still run. Existing effects keep their ordinary
  lifecycle. `--hold-effects` only pauses claims and keeps effects claimable
  later; `--hold-schedules` only holds admission. `--replay` is one spelling
  for the no-notifications replay task, rather than a second independent
  suppression flag. It is refused outside `dev` or with `--release`
  (`E_REPLAY_DEV_ONLY`); production always emits normally.
- **Expo:** `init --expo` writes the Metro configuration the web device's wasm
  needs.

**2026-10-07 — DK rounds 1–2: refused bearers explain themselves within the dev trust boundary.**
The authority decision and `E_AUTH`/`auth` envelope stay unchanged. Detailed
wording requires both dev mode and the same loopback peer/Host/Origin check as
dev-only endpoints. Declared public POST routes bypass dev admission, so they
must explicitly apply that check before choosing an explanation. Serve and
untrusted dev requests use identical text for all token states: "this session
is not live; sign in again". This avoids an issued-token membership oracle.
No reason field, store identity, token or principal is added to the refusal.

After authority refuses, a read-only lookup may identify expiry from an existing
full/read-session record. A refused unexpired record can explain loss of authority.
Absent records remain ambiguous: a token may come from an earlier or replaced
store or another instance, or have expired or been signed out, including before
this server started. The repair is sign in again and discard saved tokens from
an earlier store. No token history or process cache is kept, no store format
changes, and diagnostics add or remove nothing at store open. Detached auth/poll
readers keep their existing admission ordering; lookup cannot change authority.

Identity doors (`logout`, `narrow`, `refresh`, `logout-all`) preserve the same
`Refusal` as query/schema/changes/actions: HTTP 401 for a terminal refused bearer,
`E_AUTH`/`auth`, the unprefixed message and `guide: personas`. A retryable refusal
keeps HTTP 503. Logout and narrowing still authorize inside their writer
transaction; only after a refusal does the HTTP adapter choose diagnostic prose.
A live credential of the wrong kind keeps the operation's own explanation.
Refresh losing authority between initial resolution and rotation also preserves
the envelope; it never wraps the sentence in `RuntimeError::Auth`.

SDK online/local terminal cleanup retains the validated refusal instead of
synthesizing "sign in to continue"; app fences and the online arm preserve it too.
A terminal E_AUTH during device-app restoration also enters the signed-out
facade when no valid previous owner is being restored: `app.ready`, `app.auth.why`
and `app.online` query/mutate/act retain the same explanation. Local `logoutAll`
keeps a cause already retained after session death. Successful sign-in replaces
that cause; never-signed-in clients stay generic. The first current-credential
refusal wins; obsolete rotation refusals and retryable auth failures retain their
existing rules. Ordinary signed-out clients still ask
for sign-in. No new public field or generated API shape is required; package
declaration generation checks the existing contract.

### 20.3 A Following feed that is complete and cheap is on the card (S14, S15)

Every Astra run rebuilt Following differently, and the 0.2.12 grader found
its read-time filter returning short incomplete pages at scale. The feeds
card carries one paved Following feed. It is complete at the scale envelope
(1,000 users, a 500-follow reader, sparse readers) and answers on the device.
Following a user acquires that author's recent posts; unfollowing removes
them; reposts and the reader's own posts appear. `check` notes a `where`
filter whose predicate pins nothing in the scanned index prefix, because at
scale such a filter returns short incomplete pages, and the rewrite names the
recipe. The lane records the design it chose, and the alternatives it
measured, in this section.


**Built by lane C, 2026-09-14: choose the hybrid.** The simulator seeds
1,000 author identities, exactly 50,000 source events and 1,415 follow
edges: independent 0/1/5/500-follow readers, a celebrity with 900 followers
and 200 posts, a celebrity-plus-four reader, and a five-follower writer.
All three candidates run in the same interpreter with the default meters.
Each latency is the nearest-rank p95 of 20 samples after three warm-ups,
in milliseconds on the shared development host; these are simulator
### 20.6 A read rule may name a service principal (ruling 20; S35)

A read rule may carry disjuncts `viewer = 'service:<name>'` beside its
audience rule. Services hold no partition, and the `service:` namespace is
reserved, so the sync audience is inferred from the rule with those
disjuncts removed; no device's partition changes. `check --residency` lists
the service grants. A second disjunct that is not a service principal is
still refused.

### 20.7 A public table may sync a subset to each device (ruling 21; S16)

A table whose read rule is `public` may declare a `sync` audience narrower
than the read rule (`sync to .followerId`, or an audience through another
table). A device then holds a subset of what its viewer may read. A read the
subset cannot decide is server-class, like a read past a horizon:
`complete: false` on the device, answered by the server online. A write to a
row inside the subset predicts as usual. `NOT-DOING.md` records the move in
the same change. The public-audience half of the exact-audience invariant
("never misses one it may") is given up deliberately for these tables; the
other half ("never holds a row it may not read") stands. The work lands
after wave 2.

### 20.8 The darwin binary is signed with Developer ID (ruling 22; S31)

`scripts/publish.mjs` signs the production darwin binary with the
Developer ID Application identity, with hardened runtime and a secure
timestamp, verifies the signature, and refuses to publish if signing fails.
It notarizes when a notarytool keychain profile is configured; otherwise it
says in its output that the binary is not notarized, never silently. Launch
latency under load is measured for ad-hoc against Developer ID signing and
recorded in the journal, because whether signing removes the `_dyld_start`
stall is not established.

### 20.9 Maintains that filter, compute group keys and expose an order (S24, S25, S26)

**Design proposal, 2026-09-14, lane D-design (Codex / gpt-6-astra).** The
author commissioned this section; its recommendations are not additional
rulings under §14. The implementation lane follows the current landing.
The language card and package README still describe the shipped language.

## 8. The client, dev and rule seams the runs hit

Each item names the loop it removes (§2.2).

1. **A mutation's result reaches the client.** `Write` gains
   `result` on `sent` (the server already answers with it,
   `crates/snapback4/src/serve.rs`); `useMutation().run()` resolves with
   the `Write`. Ruled (2026-09-13): `result` on `sent` only — no
   `predicted` on `pending`; a prediction is visible as `pending` rows,
   not as an answer.
   Fresh replies remove Grok's DM-reuse lookup. **2026-09-14 correction
   under LLP 3000.008's delegated program:** §17 deliberately withholds
   historical values on replay. `Write<R>` therefore distinguishes fresh
   `sent` with `result: R` (including null) from `sent` with
   `replayed: true` and no result. Both clients and hooks preserve this
   distinction; a lost acknowledgement never grants historical read
   authority or justifies resubmission with a new ID. An application may
   make a newly authorized query when it receives execution identity only.
2. **A shape over a device row keeps `pending`.** `*` spreads device
   metadata through as it spreads columns; `api.ts` types a shaped
   object with `pending?: boolean` when its base is a row. Removes the
   0.2.6 M6 loop and the `historyRows` second query.
3. **`webDevice()` persists the wasm.** The opener keeps the module's
   bytes in IndexedDB by digest and opens on them with no network, so an
   offline reload does not depend on a URL. Removes the M3 loop the
   builder solved by hand and makes the cold-offline promise the
   opener's, not the app's.
4. **The `{ id }` asset argument predicts.** The device resolves the
   uploader's own upload facts onto the argument as the server does
   (`issues/20260913-snapback4-video-id-only-prediction-refuses.md`).
5. **Identity admission under `dev`.** Ruled (2026-09-13): on loopback,
   `snapback4 dev` lifts the per-peer and per-email minute counters to
   what the host can carry — the Argon2 slots and the connection caps,
   which are the physical bounds, remain — and prints the fact once;
   `serve` is unchanged. Removes two loops in each of the Astra and
   Grok lanes and the harness's backoff scaffolding.
   **2026-10-06, HR:** password seed scripts and replay adapters use the
   existing `signup`/`login` exports from `snapback4/auth`, passing the returned
   session to one `createClient` per account. Signup already creates a live
   session. No new auth verb, credential store or development bypass is needed.
   The auth card and starter READMEs teach this; the social starter emits a
   Node script for N accounts and each account's authorized profile write.
   Reruns choose login explicitly; arbitrary signup refusals never trigger an
   automatic fallback. Tests execute the published guide and installed script,
   including fresh login, authorized writes and cross-user refusal. Existing
   Argon2, admission limits, schema opt-in and dev-only doors stay unchanged.
6. **A hidden unique clash says what it is.** The refusal stays generic
   `E_RULE` where it must (§8.7), and its message adds the one sentence
   from `why E_RULE`: "or a unique key collided with a row you cannot
   read; to write into another principal's row use `upsert` under an
   `update` rule, or let a `maintain` keep the count."
7. **Write authority is the write rule (revised after the blind review,
   §15).** What Clique's counter tables hit is the binder: a unique-key
   `update` or `upsert` reads its target under the READ rule first
   (`bind/program.rs:603–641`), so a hidden target looks absent — an
   alternate-key update is `NOT_FOUND`, an upsert inserts and collides
   with generic `E_RULE` — while a by-id `update` already fetches without
   a read check and applies the update rule (`write.rs:66–100`). Two
   lanes opened their tables to get past it. The proposal, narrowed to
   what both reviews found defensible:
   (a) **target resolution is engine-private**: a unique-key or id write
   resolves its target without the read rule, then the table's `update`
   rule decides, as Postgres applies an `UPDATE` policy without a
   `SELECT` policy. **The update rule judges old and next:** an unnamed
   `update <- R` must hold for the row before the write (the pre-write
   state) and for the merged row after it, `R[old] and R[next]`, as an
   `UPDATE` policy's `USING` judges the existing row and, with no
   `WITH CHECK`, the new row; a named `update (old, next)` judges exactly
   what it names. A rule that reads only `id` and immutable columns is
   judged once, because a patch cannot change its inputs (a hidden target
   drops immutable patch fields; a readable mismatch is refused). A denial
   follows (b): `E_RULE` on a readable target, `NOT_FOUND` on an unreadable
   one. *Fixed 2026-10-08:* until then the engine judged only the next
   image, so `update <- .owner = viewer` without `immutable owner` let any
   caller take another principal's row by writing `owner: viewer`, even a
   row it could not read. The Lean oracle found it (LLP 3000.035 §5.2,
   `lean/OPEN.md` R2); the fix is `schema/update_images.rs`, applied in
   `check_rule` on every host;
   (b) **one failure word for an unreadable target**: absence, an update
   rule that refuses, a failed `if` condition, an immutable-column
   mismatch and an incomplete patch on the insert path all answer
   `NOT_FOUND` — the zero-row update — with no `current`, no named index
   and no named column; a readable target keeps today's codes. The
   disclosure granted is exactly: a row the update rule let this writer
   modify exists, and the rule's predicates held of it;
   (c) **the merged image never leaves the engine**: a valued write's
   `result` and `E_CONFLICT`'s `current` are a read-rule `get` (null when
   hidden), never the merged row; `old` in `update (old, next)` is the
   engine's, bound nowhere in the author's program; asset facts on
   unchanged columns are preserved without re-validation, and the update
   rule is checked before any asset diagnostic (`write.rs:75–156`);
   (d) **withheld before recorded**: `_ops` stores exactly the body `/m`
   returns, so a replay cannot grow a row (the existing gap is
   `issues/20260913-snapback4-ops-replay-returns-cached-content-after-revocation.md`);
   (e) **the device never predicts against a target it does not hold**:
   a fetch miss on a write is queued without a row — no predicted
   `NOT_FOUND`, no predicted insert, no `pending` row — on both stores,
   and `admit` queues that class (today `local::predict` raises
   `E_PREDICT` only past a horizon, `admit` fails on any other refusal,
   and an upsert miss takes the insert path and plants a `pending` row);
   (f) **`insert … if absent` on a hidden collision stays `E_RULE`**
   (S05), and so does a collision with any *other* hidden row on another
   index: target authority does not transfer;
   (g) **a readable maintain over a hidden source is a declared read-rule
   channel** — a writer who may read the aggregate learns the delta they
   caused; `check` notes an update rule wider than the read rule under a
   maintain the writer can read;
   (h) `delete` is out of scope.
   Not claimed: constant time; that constraint outcomes disclose nothing
   — a cap counted over physical rows, `after insert` on the insert
   branch, a budget abort near a ceiling — which the GPT review lists and
   §15 records as residuals of the narrowed contract. Regressions: §15's
   `s05_*` and `w1_*` list. Awaits the author's ruling (§14, 15).
8. **`snapback4 sql "…"`, a fifth observability verb.** Read-only SQL
   over generated per-table views (`json_extract` over the store's
   `r(t, id, data)`, `crates/snapback4-core/src/store.rs:101`), as the
   developer over the dev store or a `--release` directory, bounded by a
   row limit; never an application surface and never rule-filtered,
   because it is the developer's own store. Answers the ground-truth
   complaint of two essays and the operations dimension (53 against 76);
   the 0.2.6 Astra lane backed up its SQLite by hand to get the same
   thing. Catalog inspection (2026-10-04) adds `\dt` / `.tables` and
   `\d <table>` / `.schema <table>` under the same verb and read-only snapshot.
   They read the active generation's application schema, never SQLite metadata:
   tables and public maintained views, Quarry types/nullability, indexes and
   unique keys (including implicit id), and stored row counts exact through
   10,000, otherwise a lower bound of 10,001. Ephemeral counts are unavailable.
   Index provenance is the source-declared identity set captured before compiler
   expansion. It is transient compiler input, excluded from schema equality,
   hashes, serialized generation schemas and device projections. A separate
   `_meta` catalog record commits atomically with successful server activation,
   tied to its generation and schema hash. An unchanged adoption can refresh
   that record without creating a generation or changing stored schema bytes
   (SX round 3; LLP 3000.022's capability-free compatibility fence).
   Source-declared unnamed unique keys remain authored, with their internal
   spelling hidden. Generated indexes have no displayed name; bookkeeping
   indexes over hidden columns are omitted. Older generations without the
   record, or a record from a different activation, report unknown provenance,
   never a name-based guess. Inspection neither writes nor compiles local source.
   Private maintained targets stay hidden. Internal-name refusals print
   "`\dt` lists tables; `\d messages` describes one". No REPL is introduced.
   `check` previews newly declared/changed sync windows with at most 10,000
   row keys per table and notes a population at least ten times the window;
   totals explicitly span all groups and do not imply a per-group overflow.
   Unchanged windows stay quiet. The sync/reads openings and starter comments
   distinguish device working sets from server history and offline acquisition.
   Ruled (2026-09-13) as a fifth named verb beside `why`,
   `trace`, `logs` and `data`; the Moves line is in `NOT-DOING.md`.
9. **`snapback4 check --fix`.** Applies the spelling-class rewrites in
   place — an ambiguous key's `by`, a cursor index's missing `id`
   tie-break, an alias to its canonical form, `proc` to `fn` — and prints
   every other diagnostic as today. The diagnostic-and-rewrite loop
   exists so an agent can apply the rewrite; the tool applying the
   mechanical ones is the loop bar's cheapest win.
10. **`snapback4 init --expo`.** The `apps/chat-expo` starter with a
    Hermes-clean toolchain pin. Grok's seven failed iOS exports were an
    Expo/Babel version mismatch in the app, not Snapback; a starter
    removes the guess and the native artifact the grade wants.
11. **`api.ts` documents itself.** A doc comment per operation: the
    arguments, the result, `runs`/`predicts`, and the `require` codes
    the program can raise, which the binder knows statically. Agents
    read `api.ts` before the README.
12. **A server exit without a diagnostic.** The 0.2.6 Astra lane's scale
    instance exited twice during a schema change with a backfill and left
    nothing in its log; filed as
    `issues/20260913-snapback4-dev-exits-without-diagnostic-during-schema-change.md`.
    A defect, not a design item; listed because "sail through" includes
    not dying silently.
13. **An SDK-managed cache for ordinary media.** Asset responses are
    `private, no-store` by design, so every local-first builder — both
    Astra runs, and the Convex and Supabase builders for their own
    reasons — wrote a per-principal media cache by hand, with its own
    purge on revocation and its own view-once exclusion. Proposed: the
    local-first client keeps the bytes of ordinary `image`/`video`
    assets it has fetched, keyed by asset id and home row, in the
    device's own storage (IndexedDB on the web, the documents directory
    under the native module), with explicit retention (`assets: { keep:
    "viewed" | "none", maxBytes }`), purged when the home row leaves the
    partition, is cleared, expires or is deleted, and never for a `once`
    asset. `useAsset` reads the cache first offline. This is the
    residency draft's "ordinary media durability" gap and the received
    review's second-phase item; it makes the cold-offline promise the
    client's rather than the app's, as §8.3 does for the wasm. Ruled by
    the author on 2026-09-13: it lands with the language (§12, A).

    **2026-09-22 native compatibility:** fetched React Native Blobs may lack
    `arrayBuffer`; the shared SDK uses public FileReader and releases its
    owned response Blob after copying. A transient once handle may use an
    in-memory data URI if the host's object-URL API fails; copied strings
    must be dropped by the caller on close and cannot be forcibly revoked.
    Once bytes still never enter durable media storage. The first-party
    Swift store gives admitted MP4 a real `.mp4` filename for AVFoundation,
    migrating legacy bare-ID files within the same private directory. An
    atomically written bare file wins interrupted dual-name states; purge
    removes the possible shadow before that authoritative file. Images keep
    bare IDs, and close preserves retained files. This uses the existing
    store lock and identity validation, without another display cache or ABI.
    [LLP 3000.011.005.000 §8](./3000.011.005.000-qualify-the-built-application.rfc.md#8-actual-app-qualification-exposed-a-native-media-defect)
    records the actual-host failures, selected remedies and qualification.

## 9. Escape hatches for the last ten percent

**2026-09-16 update:** application SQL reads are admitted (LLP 3000.009
§14.4). The original proposal and its costs below remain as design history;
LLP 3000.009 §6.2 supersedes its SQL representation, authorization and limits.
Implementation is pending in that RFC's increment D, on both stores.

    pub(super) fn refuse_engine_owned(&self, table: &str, effect: Effect) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — pending member changes cannot rewrite settled requirements.
        if self.device && effect != Effect::Insert && self.schema.receipts.iter().any(|f| f.members == table || f.runs == table) {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("receipt membership changes and progress queue until settlement".into()));
        }
        self.refuse_receipt_table(table)?;
        self.refuse_condition_write()?;
        self.refuse_timeline_write(table, effect)?;
        self.schema.refuse_private(table)?;
        if self.schema.maintain_for(table).is_some() {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{table} is a maintained aggregate; write its source rows instead")));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

                    && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, old)?

            _ => true };

                if old.is_some_and(|old| index_values(index, old) == key) { continue; }
                if key.iter().any(|value| *value == Value::Null) {

                refusal.retryable = true;

                refusal.rewrite = Some("retry after the server publishes the next bounded opening".into());
            }
            Self::Store(_) => refusal.retryable = true,
            Self::Asset { message, .. } => {
                refusal.message = message.clone();
                refusal.guide = Some("assets".into());
            }
            Self::Native { message, .. } => {
                refusal.message = message.clone();
                refusal.guide = Some("native".into());
                };
                Ok((domain, Ty::Int))
            }
            A::Name { name, site } if self.scopes[0].contains_key(name) && self.binding(name).is_some_and(|binding| binding.runtime == *name) => {
                let ty = self.lookup(name).expect("bound argument").clone();
                match ty {
                    Ty::List(item, max) => Ok((LoopDomain::ArgList { name: name.clone(), max }, *item)),
                    Ty::Optional(inner) if matches!(*inner, Ty::List(..)) => Err(type_error(site, "for cannot iterate an optional list", format!("for x in {name} ?? []:"))),
                    other => Err(type_error(site, format!("for cannot iterate {}", other.name()), "iterate a bounded page or a bounded list argument")),
                }
            }
            other => {
                let (expr, ty) = self.expr(other, out)?;
                match ty {
                    Ty::List(item, max) => Ok((LoopDomain::DerivedArray { value: expr, max, bound_source: "list".into() }, *item)),
                    Ty::Page(table, max) => Ok((LoopDomain::DerivedArray { value: expr, max, bound_source: "page".into() }, Ty::Row(table))),
                    Ty::Collection(item, max) => Ok((LoopDomain::DerivedArray { value: expr, max, bound_source: "shape".into() }, *item)),
                    Ty::Optional(inner) if inner.loop_max().is_some() => Err(type_error(other.site(), "for cannot iterate an optional list", format!("for x in {} ?? []:", print::expression(other)))),
                    Ty::Unknown => Err(unbound_loop(other.site(), "for cannot prove a static bound for this value", "iterate a bounded page, a bounded list argument, or tokens(text)")),
                    other_ty => Err(type_error(other.site(), format!("for cannot iterate {}", other_ty.name()), "iterate a bounded page or bounded list")),
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// Arguments belong to the caller: bind and snapshot each one before
    /// introducing any parameter. `new` and reads are evaluated once, in
    /// source order, even when the helper uses the parameter repeatedly.
    fn helper_arguments(&mut self, name: &str, declared: &[ast::ArgDecl], args: &[A], site: &Site, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<BTreeMap<String, Binding>> {
        if self.depth >= MAX_EXPANSION_DEPTH {
            return Err(unsupported(site, "helpers nested deeper than eight levels", "flatten the helper"));
        }
        if args.len() != declared.len() {
            return Err(type_error(site, format!("{name} takes {} arguments; received {}", declared.len(), args.len()), format!("{name}({})", declared.iter().map(|a| a.name.clone()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", "))));
        }
        let mut bindings = BTreeMap::new();
        for (declared, given) in declared.iter().zip(args) {
            if bindings.contains_key(&declared.name) {
                return Err(unknown(&declared.site, format!("duplicate argument {}", declared.name), "rename one helper parameter"));
            }
            let expected = Ty::from_scalar(&declared.type_);
            // Helpers are polymorphic over same-table row snapshots; retain their
            // existing row parameter semantics. Only a literal needs id conversion.
            let (expr, ty) = if expected.required().is_identity() && matches!(given, A::Literal { .. }) { self.expr_as_identity(given, out, &expected)? } else { self.expr(given, out)? };
            // @ref LLP 3000.007#18.5 — call-site expansion preserves a same-table row; references keep their existing meaning.
            let expected = match (expected.required(), ty.required()) {
                (Ty::Ref(table), Ty::Row(row)) if table == row && (!ty.is_optional() || expected.is_optional()) => {
                    if expected.is_optional() { Ty::Row(row).optional() } else { Ty::Row(row) }
                }
                (Ty::Ref(table), Ty::WriteRow(row)) if table == row && (!ty.is_optional() || expected.is_optional()) => {
                    if expected.is_optional() { Ty::WriteRow(row).optional() } else { Ty::WriteRow(row) }
                }
                _ => expected,
            };
            if !ty.assignable_to(&expected) {
                return Err(type_error(given.site(), format!("{name}'s {} is {}; got {}", declared.name, expected.name(), ty.name()), match (ty.required(), expected.required()) {
                    (Ty::Enum(variants), Ty::Text(max)) if variants.iter().any(|variant| variant.chars().count() > max as usize) => format!("change {name}'s parameter to `{}: {}`; not every variant fits text <={max}", declared.name, ty.name()),
                    _ if ty.is_optional() && !expected.is_optional() => self.parent_rewrite(given).unwrap_or_else(|| format!("{} — require this argument once before calling {name}; absent or hidden rows refuse NOT_FOUND", print::expression(&A::Assert { value: Box::new(given.clone()), code: "NOT_FOUND".into(), message: None, site: given.site().clone() }))),
                    _ => format!("pass {} for {}; a table parameter receives an id when called with a reference, or the same-table row snapshot when called with a row. To read fields from an id, bind `{table}[{}] ! else NOT_FOUND` in the helper; multiline fn bodies need `return value`", expected.name(), declared.name, declared.name, table = match expected.required() { Ty::Ref(t) => t, _ => "<table>".into() }),
                }));
            }
            let runtime = self.temp(&declared.name);
            self.maintenance_scopes.insert(runtime.clone(), format!("helper/{name}/parameter/{}", declared.name));
            out.push(Stmt::Let { name: runtime.clone(), value: expr });
            bindings.insert(declared.name.clone(), Binding { runtime, ty: expected.clone(), declared: expected, parameter: true, revision: 0, fields: BTreeMap::new(), error: None, origins: Vec::new() });
        }
        Ok(bindings)
    }

    pub(super) fn fn_call(&mut self, function: &ast::FunctionDecl, args: &[A], site: &Site, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
        let bindings = self.helper_arguments(&function.name, &function.args, args, site, out)?;
        let start = out.len();
        let caller = std::mem::replace(&mut self.scopes, vec![bindings]);
        self.declare(pure_calls::CONSTANTS, Ty::Null);
        let focal = self.focal.take();
        let loops = std::mem::take(&mut self.loops);
        // @ref LLP 3000.019#6 — remove the measured helper/inline placement discrepancy.
        // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.2 — placement inherits caller loops; break/continue stay lexical.
        self.caller_loops += loops;
        let returns = std::mem::take(&mut self.returns);
        self.depth += 1;
        self.call_chain.push((function.name.clone(), site.clone()));
        // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.2 — helpers expand in the caller's placement; a return exits only this expansion.
        let result = match &function.body {
            ast::FunctionBody::Expression(value) => self.value_of(value, out),
            ast::FunctionBody::Block(statements) => {
                let mut body = setup::Body::default();
                self.block(statements, &mut body, false).and_then(|()| {
                    let ty = self.return_type()?;
                    let result = self.temp("result");
                    self.maintenance_scopes.insert(result.clone(), format!("helper/{}/result", function.name));
                    let done = self.temp("returned");
                    out.push(Stmt::Let { name: result.clone(), value: Expr::Literal(Value::Null) });
                    out.push(Stmt::Let { name: done.clone(), value: Expr::Literal(Value::Bool(false)) });
                    let ownership = setup::helper_ownership(&body);
                    let code = helper_returns(body.code, &result, &done).0;
                    out.extend(setup::Body { code, ownership });
                    Ok((ir::var(&result), ty))
                })
            }
        };

    fn key_ty(&self, info: &TableInfo, index: &ast::IndexDecl, column: &str) -> Ty {
        if index.computed.contains_key(column) { return Ty::Int; }
        if column == "id" {
            return Ty::Ref(info.decl.name.clone());
        }
        info.columns.get(column).map(Ty::from_scalar).unwrap_or(Ty::Unknown)
    }

    fn order_keys(&mut self, info: &TableInfo, index: &ast::IndexDecl, keys: Vec<(Option<String>, Expr, Ty)>) -> Fallible<Vec<Expr>> {
        let named = keys.iter().all(|(c, _, _)| c.is_some());
        if !named {
            for (position, (_, _, t)) in keys.iter().enumerate() {
                let expected = self.key_ty(info, index, &index.columns[position]);
                if !t.comparable(&expected) {
                    return Err(type_error(&index.site, format!("key {} is {}; {}.{}.{} is {}", position + 1, t.name(), info.decl.name, index.name, index.columns[position], expected.name()), format!("use {} for key {}", expected.name(), position + 1)));
                }
            }
            return Ok(keys.into_iter().map(|(_, e, _)| e).collect());
        }
        let mut ordered = Vec::new();
        for column in index.columns.iter().take(keys.len()) {
            let Some(position) = keys.iter().position(|(c, _, _)| c.as_deref() == Some(column)) else {
                return Err(unknown(&index.site, format!("key omits column {column} of {}.{}", info.decl.name, index.name), format!("name each prefix column once: {}", index.columns.iter().take(keys.len()).cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", "))));
            };
            let expected = self.key_ty(info, index, column);
            if !keys[position].2.comparable(&expected) {
                return Err(type_error(&index.site, format!("{column} is {}; {}.{column} is {}", keys[position].2.name(), info.decl.name, expected.name()), format!("use {} for {column}", expected.name())));
            }
            ordered.push(keys[position].1.clone());
        }
        Ok(ordered)
    }

    fn walk(&mut self, table: &str, seed: &A, column: &str, depth: u32, site: &Site, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<(Recurse, Ty)> {
        let info = self.table(table, site)?;
        let Some(next) = info.columns.get(column) else {
            return Err(unknown(site, format!("{table} has no column {column}"), name_rewrite(column, info.columns.keys().map(String::as_str), None)));
        };
        if !matches!(next.kind, ast::TypeKind::Ref { table: ref t } if t == table) {
            return Err(type_error(site, format!("walk follows a reference back to {table}; {table}.{column} is {}", print::scalar_type(next)), format!("{column}: {table} ?")));
        }
        if depth == 0 || depth > 64 {
            return Err(unbound_loop(site, "walk depth is between 1 and 64", format!("walk {table}[seed] up .{column} depth 8")));
        }
        let (seed_expr, _) = self.expr_as_identity(seed, out, &Ty::Ref(table.to_owned()))?;
        Ok((Recurse { site: self.site(), table: table.to_owned(), index: "byId".into(), seed: Box::new(seed_expr), next_field: column.to_owned(), depth, fanout: 1, provenance: KeyProvenance::Computed }, Ty::Row(table.to_owned())))
    }

    fn merge(&mut self, merge: &ast::MergeExpr, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
        if merge.lanes.iter().any(|lane| lane.planned.is_some()) || merge.index.is_empty() { return self.planned_view(merge, out, prefix::Position::Page); }
        let info = self.table(&merge.table, &merge.site)?;
        if merge.lanes.first().and_then(|lane| lane.table.as_deref()).is_some_and(|table| table != merge.table) {
            return Err(type_error(&merge.site, "the first merge lane must use the header table, which owns the cursor", "start with [prefix] for the header table").guide("feeds"));
        }
        let Some(index) = info.indexes.iter().find(|index| index.name == merge.index).cloned() else {
            return Err(unknown(&merge.site, format!("{} has no index {}", merge.table, merge.index), name_rewrite(&merge.index, info.indexes.iter().map(|i| i.name.as_str()), None)));
        };

        let direction = if merge.order == ast::Order::Asc { "first" } else { "last" };

        if let Some((position, _)) = &index.words {
            let scope = &index.columns[..*position];
        if super::columns::fields(info).next().is_some() { Ty::WriteRow(info.decl.name.clone()) } else { Ty::Row(info.decl.name.clone()) }
    }

    fn calendar_number(&self, value: &A, depth: u8) -> bool {
        if depth > 8 { return false; }
        match value {
            A::Call { name, .. } => matches!(name.as_str(), "day" | "hour" | "bucket"),
            A::Name { name, .. } => self.binding(name).is_some_and(|binding| binding.revision == 0 && binding.origins.len() == 1 && self.calendar_number(&binding.origins[0].1, depth + 1)),
            A::If { then, otherwise, .. } => self.calendar_number(then, depth + 1) || self.calendar_number(otherwise, depth + 1),
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    fn field_value(&mut self, field: &ObjectField, expected: &Ty, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
        if expected.required() == Ty::Time && field.value.as_ref().map_or_else(
            || self.calendar_number(&A::Name { name: field.name.clone(), site: field.site.clone() }, 0), |value| self.calendar_number(value, 0)) {
            return Err(type_error(&field.site, "day/hour/bucket returns a period number, not a time in milliseconds",
                "store the period number in an int field, or use day(now) * 1d for a UTC midnight time (hour(now) * 1h for an hour)"));
        }
        match &field.value {
            Some(value) if expected.required().is_identity() => self.expr_as_identity(value, out, expected),
            Some(value) => {
                let (e, t) = self.expr(value, out)?;
                // A text literal in an enum position is that variant.
                if let (Ty::Enum(variants), Expr::Literal(Value::String(text))) = (expected.required(), &e) {
                    if variants.contains(text) {
                        return Ok((e, Ty::Enum(variants)));
                    }
                    return Err(type_error(value.site(), format!("'{text}' is not one of {}", variants.iter().map(|v| format!("'{v}'")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")), format!("'{}'", variants.first().cloned().unwrap_or_default())));
                }
                Ok((e, t))
            }
            None => {
                let (value, ty) = self.name(&field.name, &field.site)?;
                Ok(self.row_identity(value, ty, expected))
            },
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum ReadMode {
    /// A full unique key: one row.
    pub(super) fn call(&mut self, name: &str, args: &[A], site: &Site, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
        if let Some(result) = self.job_query_call(name, args, site, out) { return result; }
        // Compiler-only references bypass the function catalog entirely.
        let primitive = name.strip_prefix("$builtin:");
        if primitive.is_none() && let Some(function) = self.catalog.functions.get(name).cloned() {
            return self.fn_call(&function, args, site, out);
        }
        let name = primitive.unwrap_or(name);
        let arity = |n: usize, rewrite: &str| -> Fallible<()> {
            if args.len() != n {
                return Err(type_error(site, format!("{name} takes {n} argument{}; received {}", if n == 1 { "" } else { "s" }, args.len()), rewrite));
            }
            Ok(())
        };
        match name {
            "receiptSettled" if primitive.is_some() => {
                arity(1, "receipt settlement needs a row")?;
                let (value, ty) = self.expr(&args[0], out)?;
                let Ty::Row(table) = ty else { return Err(type_error(site, "receipt settlement needs a row", "use a receipt row")); };
                Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::ReceiptSettled { table }, args: vec![value] }, Ty::Bool))
            }
            super::super::intent_variants::PRESENT => {
                let (value, _) = self.expr(&args[0], out)?;
                Ok((Expr::Binary { op: BinaryOp::Ne, left: Box::new(value), right: Box::new(Expr::Literal(Value::Null)) }, Ty::Bool))
            }
            super::super::intent_variants::SEARCH => {
                let (value, ty) = self.expr(&args[0], out)?;
                if !matches!(ty, Ty::Text(_)) { return Err(type_error(site, "matching needs present text", "matching (q ?? '')")); }
                let A::Name { name, .. } = &args[1] else { unreachable!("planned needle binding") };
                let runtime = self.temp("intentNeedle");
                self.declare(name, ty);
                self.scopes.last_mut().unwrap().get_mut(name).unwrap().runtime = runtime.clone();
                out.push(Stmt::Let { name: runtime.clone(), value });
                Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::SearchPresent, args: vec![ir::var(&runtime)] }, Ty::Bool))
            }
            "day" | "hour" | "bucket" => {

                let (value, ty) = self.expr(&args[0], out)?;
                if ty != Ty::Time { return Err(type_error(args[0].site(), format!("{name} needs a required time, got {}", ty.name()), "pass a required time column or now")); }

//! Compiled examples first; diagnostic details are under `why`.
pub(super) const CARD: &str = r##"# Programs

Queries read data; mutations change it in one transaction.
Jobs run background work, and helpers share logic between programs.

```quarry
query programForms(roomId: rooms):                             -- reads only; the last expression, or `return`, is the result, typed onto api.ts
  rooms[roomId] card

mutation programWrites(roomId: rooms, title: text 1..80):     -- reads and writes in one transaction, at most once per client-minted id
  room = rooms[roomId] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require room.ownerId = viewer else NOT_OWNER
  update rooms[room] { name: title }                           -- a final write is the implicit return
```

`programForms` returns the `card` shape; `programWrites` checks visibility
and ownership before renaming.
Helpers share one namespace; a helper from `m.q` accepts both `helper(x)` and `m.helper(x)`.
A different module name is refused with the declaring file and the correct call.
Helpers inherit loop placement (guide jobs); repeated pure calls narrow (guide types).

## Limits

- Queries cannot write or mint ids, including through helpers: E_QUARRY_PLACEMENT.
- Mutation scans need an authorized scope: E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT.
- Application refusal codes cannot start with `E_`: E_OP_RESERVED.

## Details

Queries read data; mutations change it in one transaction.
Jobs run background work, and helpers share logic between programs.

### Loop writes

Read an authorized page, then write each row:
Mutation scans of expiring tables require `predicts: "never"` —
inferred from server-only work, or declared with `: server` — and must sit in
the initial read-only phase. A write or emit anywhere in an enclosing statement
ends it. Bind before writing loops:

```quarry
table expiringNotes:
  owner: principal
  body: text <=200
  expiresAt: time ?
  read <- .owner = viewer
  update <- .owner = viewer
  expire at .expiresAt
  sync to .owner last 100 by .id

mutation annotateNotes(): server
  page = expiringNotes where .owner = viewer first 10 by .id
  for row in page:
    update expiringNotes[row] { body: 'read' }
  return null
```

Pages still need uniform plain prefixes; unswept expired rows cost no meter
(guide bounds).

### App files and modules

```
my-app/
  snapback/schema.q          the backend: tables, rules, sync, queries, mutations
  snapback/workers/push.mjs  declared Node worker; dev and serve start it (guide effects: ledger: true)
  snapback/worker.mts        optional single Node ESM worker: effects and actions (dev starts it)
  snapback/generated/package.json  ESM boundary for generated artifacts
  snapback/generated/api.ts  written by `check`; never edited, never committed
  src/                       your client: React on the web, React Native on Expo
```

A backend shares one namespace of tables, shapes and helpers across `.q`
files. `snapback/schema.q` supplies root operations; `snapback/social.q`
supplies `api.social.<op>`. Import the generated `api` and use one client.
`sync` declares which devices hold rows and answer local reads; there are
no resolvers, migrations or subscriptions to manage.

**Two ways to run.** `snapback4 init` starts local-first: declare `sync` and
pass a device to `createApp` for offline data. `init --online` creates
`src/client.ts` without a device or `sync`; server queries stay live through
`/changes`. Both share rules, meters, identity, assets and jobs. Add a device
and `sync` later. `init --expo` selects native when available, online in Expo Go.
Starters, `check` and `dev` write `snapback/generated/package.json` with
`{"type":"module"}`: Node ESM seeds can import `api.ts` even in a CommonJS
app. Other scripts retain their module interpretation; Expo's `worker.mts`
explicitly uses ESM.

"##;
//! Identity and developer inspection.
pub(super) const CARD: &str = r##"# Personas

Password accounts work headlessly in Node and browsers; personas are named development users. Both exercise
application rules with their own principal.

```quarry
use personas alice, bob
use identity password

query whoAmI():
  return viewer
```

An email-and-password product declares `use identity password`; plain `use identity` also mints guest sessions.
`use identity guests` admits only guests; without `use identity`, both methods are disabled.

## Seed accounts headlessly

Run `snapback4 check` then `snapback4 dev` with the schema above. Save as `seed.mjs` beside `snapback/`.
Set `SEED_PASSWORD` privately and run `node seed.mjs` (Node 24). Signup returns a session; use `SEED_AUTH=login` for existing accounts (duplicate signup refuses).

```js
import { signup, login } from "snapback4/auth";
import { createClient } from "snapback4/client";
import { api } from "./snapback/generated/api.ts";
const url = process.env.SNAPBACK_URL ?? "http://127.0.0.1:4400";
const password = process.env.SEED_PASSWORD;
if (!password) throw Error("Set SEED_PASSWORD");
const mode = process.env.SEED_AUTH ?? "signup";
if (mode !== "signup" && mode !== "login") throw Error("SEED_AUTH must be signup or login");
const authenticate = mode === "signup" ? signup : login;
const result = await authenticate(url, "seed1@example.test", password);
if (!result.ok) throw Error(result.why.message);
const client = createClient({ url, session: result.session });
try {
  const me = await client.query(api.whoAmI, {});
  if ("denied" in me) throw Error(me.denied.message);
  console.log(client.viewer()); // Only the principal, never the bearer.
} finally { await client.signOut(); }
```

Use `client.mutate(api.operation, args)` for writes; require `state: "sent"` or handle `"failed"` with `why`;
`"pending"` is not success. Use one client per account. The social starter's `scripts/seed.mjs` creates N users
and profiles; replay adapters use the same path. No browser, borrowed token, persona or `/seed` is needed.
SDK calls POST `{email, password}` to `/auth/signup` or `/auth/login`: `{ok: true, session}` or `{ok: false, why}`
(wire: `{session}` or `{denied}`). Use HTTPS off loopback. There is no `snapback4 auth create`; `run --as` and `/seed` do not create password credentials.

Ordinary guest and password sessions last seven days. `refreshSession` atomically exchanges a live token;
`logoutAll` revokes every session for the principal. The client refreshes near expiry and uses an in-memory
session store by default. Both online and local clients expose `session()`, `onSession`, `refreshSession()` and
`logoutAll()`: rotation adopts the bearer before notification, and sign-out or a current-session refusal clears
it. Local `signOut()` fences late refresh responses and completes only after persisted credentials are removed.
Remote logout is best effort and does not gate that local boundary. An in-flight rotation may return its
successor for logout, but cannot adopt or persist it after sign-out. Storage failure rejects sign-out for retry;
`close()` alone preserves the session. Neither operation erases the outbox. Personas have no session; a
bare-token online client has none until refresh returns one. Only the local client has `sync()`.
`localStorageSessionStore()` is an explicit compatibility choice whose token can be read by same-origin script;
native apps should pass their secure store.

Trusted dev E_AUTH explains expiry or possible causes for unknown tokens; the SDK keeps the message.
Sign in again and discard earlier-store tokens. Serve and untrusted dev requests keep causes generic.
See `guide services` for diagnostic limits and `guide jobs` for isolated time-travel tests.

## Operations
`use personas alice, bob` declares a development cast. `snapback4 run send '{..}' --as alice` (the default
persona is alice) and the `x-snapback-persona: alice` header in development act as `dev:alice`; `persona: "alice"` on the client sends the header. A React/Expo dev UI keeps `AppProvider` and `useAuth` with
`createApp({ url, persona: "alice", device })`, one app per persona (`usePersonaApp(persona, openApp)` opens it and closes it on switch; web `?as=` and React Native pickers: "Personas in a React UI" in CLIENT-AND-OPERATIONS.md;
`init --web`/`--expo` writes one beside a schema without `use identity`, and `init --adapt` rewrites an unmodified guest starter screen into one). No session: `app.auth` sign-in, `auth.guest()` too, refuses `E_AUTH`.
The declaration is the cast: dev refuses a persona it does not name with 401 E_AUTH, naming the line to extend, so
an acceptance test can expect an outsider to be refused (a schema without `use personas` admits any name). Personas are a development door: the socket peer, `Host`, and optional
browser `Origin` must all be literal loopback/local http(s) values. Foreign, opaque, malformed and duplicate
Origins are refused before routing, and CORS reflects only an admitted local Origin. `snapback4 dev` is
development only: it admits loopback personas and an unauthenticated `POST /seed` as the system principal;
deploy with `snapback4 deploy` + `snapback4 serve`. A deployed server (`snapback4 serve`) refuses personas and
seed, defaults to `127.0.0.1`, and requires `--i-understand-cleartext` for a non-loopback HTTP bind. Put a TLS
terminator in front, preserve `Authorization` and `Origin`, strip persona headers, and rate-limit there by the
actual client address; the binary trusts only its socket peer.

`GET /auth/config` is the small public advertisement for guest/password support. Catalog, schema, generated API,
native module and changes require a live principal. Signup requires at least 8 characters (Unicode scalar
values) and at most 1,024 UTF-8 bytes; login accepts at most 1,024 UTF-8 bytes. Password hashing runs in bounded
concurrent slots outside the engine mutex. Under `serve`, guest, login and signup share 30 attempts per socket
peer per minute, while login and signup also share 10 per normalized email per minute (E_RATE_LIMIT). Under
`dev`, loopback peers have neither minute counter; their Argon2 slots equal the host's available cores, capped
at 16 and never below 2. Startup prints the slot count and the lifted counters once. `serve` and non-loopback
peers keep two slots and the minute counters; full slots refuse with retryable E_RATE_LIMIT. Connection/worker
caps remain. Unknown emails perform the same Argon2 verification work. Retry after the minute counter or
concurrent-slot pressure clears; do not retry in a tight loop.

Use `snapback4 dev --replay` when new effects must be never delivered: writes and meters remain,
new effects are counted as suppressed, and schedule admission is held. Previously queued effects remain.
`--hold-effects` instead keeps effects claimable after restarting without the flag; `--hold-schedules`
only holds schedule admission. Both schedule holds skip missed periods; a restart without `--replay` restores normal emission for new writes and keeps the count.
The policy persists for local `run` until the next host start; suppressed effects never return.
`serve` and release commands refuse `--replay` with E_REPLAY_DEV_ONLY; production always emits normally.
See `guide jobs` for full replay semantics and the disposable-store recipe.

`snapback4 sql "SELECT * FROM messages" [--limit N] [--json]` inspects the developer's own dev store; `--release
dir` selects a deployment. It opens read-only alongside the running server and is never rule-filtered. Only
application-table views are exposed; internal tables and raw r/i are refused. Views and `data` include absent
required literal defaults; optional columns stay null. Device persistence exports retain raw storage images. The
default SELECT limit is 200, with a notice when more rows exist. `snapback4 sql '\dt'` (or `'.tables'`) lists
application tables and maintained views; `sql '\d messages'` (or `'.schema messages'`) describes Quarry
columns/nullability, indexes and unique keys. Both report the active schema generation and bounded stored row
counts: exact through 10,000, otherwise >=10,001; ephemeral counts are unavailable. `--json` returns
`generation`, `tables` and `ruleFiltered: false`. These catalog commands use the active schema, even with broken
local source.

## Refusals
E_SQL_READ_ONLY means inspection received something other than one read-only `SELECT` or `WITH ... SELECT`. For
example, `snapback4 sql "DELETE FROM messages"` cannot delete rows. Use `snapback4 sql "SELECT * FROM messages"`
to inspect them, and a declared mutation for an application write. Do not combine statements or use attachment,
pragmas or side-effect functions through this inspection verb.

E_SQL_INTERNAL means inspection tried to read engine-private storage. For example, `SELECT * FROM r` or `SELECT
* FROM sqlite_master` is not an application-table view. `\dt` lists tables; `\d messages` describes one: use
`snapback4 sql '\dt'` or `snapback4 sql '\d messages'`. These views expose the developer's store, including
interpreted defaults, and are not an application authorization boundary. Use Quarry for application reads."##;

//! Bind key operands once, retaining authored sequencing and contextual literals.
use super::*;

impl<'a> Binder<'a> {
    pub(super) fn bind_key_parts(&mut self, info: &TableInfo, read: &ReadExpr, end: usize,
        keys: &mut Vec<(Option<String>, Expr, Ty)>, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<()> {
        for part in &read.keys[keys.len()..end] {
            let mut setup = setup::Body::default();
            let expected = part.column.as_deref().and_then(|column| key_identity(info, column));
            let (e, t) = match expected {
                Some(expected) => self.expr_as_identity(&part.value, &mut setup, &expected)?,
                None => self.expr(&part.value, &mut setup)?,
            };
            self.sequence_setup(keys.iter_mut().map(|(_, e, _)| e), setup, out);
            let e = if expr::allocates(&e) { self.snapshot(e, out) } else { e };
            keys.push((part.column.clone(), e, t));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    // Mixed-key normalization names an already-bound positional prefix. Only
    // a literal acquires new context; compound expressions keep their IR/setup.
    pub(super) fn name_bound_keys(&mut self, info: &TableInfo, read: &ReadExpr,
        keys: &mut [(Option<String>, Expr, Ty)]) -> Fallible<()> {
        for ((column, expr, ty), part) in keys.iter_mut().zip(&read.keys) {
            *column = part.column.clone();
            if let Some(expected) = column.as_deref().and_then(|column| key_identity(info, column))
                && matches!(&part.value, A::Literal { value: Literal::Str(_), .. }) {
                (*expr, *ty) = self.expr_as_identity(&part.value, &mut setup::Body::default(), &expected)?;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

fn key_identity(info: &TableInfo, column: &str) -> Option<Ty> {
    let ty = if column == "id" { Ty::Ref(info.decl.name.clone()) }
        else { Ty::from_scalar(info.columns.get(column)?) };
    ty.is_identity().then_some(ty)
}
//! Job viewer scopes and calls to the same declared queries used by clients.
use super::*;

pub(super) fn diagnostic(site: &Site, code: &str, message: &str, rewrite: &str) -> Diagnostic {
    Diagnostic::new(site, code, message, rewrite).guide("jobs")
}
pub(super) fn read_only(site: &Site) -> Diagnostic {
    diagnostic(site, "E_JOB_VIEWER_READ_ONLY", "as is read-only: writes, emits, new ids and once asset consumption have side effects", "compute inside as; act outside the block")
}

impl Binder<'_> {
    // @ref LLP 3000.007#21.12 — viewer scopes are read-only, under the job's transaction and meter.
    pub(super) fn as_viewer(&mut self, principal: &A, body: &[S], site: &Site, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<()> {
        if self.caller_kind != ProgramKind::Job || self.in_prelude || self.loops + self.caller_loops == 0 || self.viewer_depth.is_some() {
            return Err(diagnostic(site, "E_JOB_VIEWER_CONTEXT", "as belongs inside a job sweep and cannot nest", "put as recipient.principal: inside for recipient in recipients:"));
        }
        let (value, ty) = self.expr(principal, out)?;
        if !matches!(ty, Ty::Principal) && !matches!(principal, A::Literal { value: Literal::Str(s), .. } if snapback4_core::value::identity_fits(s) && s != snapback4_core::SYSTEM_PRINCIPAL) {
            return Err(diagnostic(principal.site(), "E_JOB_VIEWER_PRINCIPAL", "as requires a present non-system principal", "use a principal column or argument; keep intentional system reads outside as"));
        }
        let loops = self.loops;
        self.loops = 0;
        self.caller_loops += loops;
        self.clear_authority_refinements();
        self.viewer_depth = Some(self.depth);
        let mut code = setup::Body::default();
        let result = self.block(body, &mut code, false);
        self.clear_authority_refinements();
        self.viewer_depth = None;
        self.loops = loops;
        self.caller_loops -= loops;
        result?;
        out.push(Stmt::Let { name: self.temp("as"), value: Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::JobAs, args: vec![value, Expr::Block { body: code.code, value: Box::new(ir::lit(Value::Null)) }] } });
        Ok(())
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.007#21.12 — calls are reevaluated under the new viewer,
    // including implicit/transitive helper dependencies. Snapshot fields stay
    // valid. Conservatively discard call, point and maintained-authorization
    // facts at both authority edges.
    fn clear_authority_refinements(&mut self) {
        self.call_types.clear();
        for scope in &mut self.scopes {
            for binding in scope.values_mut() {
                binding.fields.retain(|path, _| path.first().is_none_or(|part| {
                    part != "$pureCall"
                        && part != "$point"
                        && part != maintain_types::AUTHORIZATION
                }));
            }
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn job_query_call(&mut self, name: &str, args: &[A], site: &Site, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Option<Fallible<(Expr, Ty)>> {
        if self.viewer_depth.is_none() || self.catalog.functions.contains_key(name) { return None; }
        let all = name == "$jobAll" && self.viewer_depth.is_some();
        let (name, args) = if all {
            match args { [A::Call { name, args, .. }] => (name.as_str(), args.as_slice()), _ => return Some(Err(diagnostic(site, "E_JOB_VIEWER_QUERY", "all takes a declared paged query call", "for row in all(unreadPreview(periodStart, periodEnd, null)):"))) }
        } else { (name, args) };
        if name == "all" && self.viewer_depth.is_some() { return Some(Err(diagnostic(site, "E_JOB_VIEWER_QUERY", "all is a streaming for domain", "for row in all(queryName(..., null)):"))); }
        if self.viewer_depth.is_some() && matches!(name, "consume" | "consumeOnce") { return Some(Err(read_only(site))); }
        let caller_module = std::path::Path::new(&site.file).file_stem().and_then(|s| s.to_str()).unwrap_or("schema");
        let (module, decl) = self.catalog.documents.iter().find_map(|doc| {
            let module = std::path::Path::new(&doc.file).file_stem()?.to_str()?;
            doc.programs.iter().find(|decl| super::super::operation_name(module, &decl.name) == name || module == caller_module && decl.name == name).map(|decl| (module.to_owned(), decl.clone()))
        })?;
        Some((|| {
            if self.viewer_depth.is_none() || decl.kind != ProgramKind::Query || decl.native || decl.held {
                return Err(diagnostic(site, "E_JOB_VIEWER_QUERY", "only declared Quarry queries may be called inside a job as block", "compute with a query inside as; call mutations, actions and native operations outside it"));
            }
            let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
            let query = Binder::bind(self.catalog, self.schema, &module, &decl, &mut diagnostics)
                .ok_or_else(|| diagnostics.into_iter().next().unwrap_or_else(|| diagnostic(site, "E_JOB_VIEWER_QUERY", "query could not be bound", "fix the declared query first")))?;
            if snapback4_core::ir::read_sites(&query.program).iter().any(|read| self.schema.table(&read.table).is_some_and(|table| table.ephemeral.is_some())) {
                return Err(diagnostic(site, "E_JOB_VIEWER_QUERY", "job viewer queries read durable data", "keep ephemeral reads in a client query; persist the state the job needs"));
            }
            if args.len() != query.args.len() { return Err(type_error(site, format!("{name} takes {} arguments", query.args.len()), "pass the same positional arguments as the declared query, including its cursor")); }
            let mut fields = BTreeMap::new();
            for ((name, expected), given) in query.args.iter().zip(args) {
                let (value, ty) = if expected.required().is_identity() { self.expr_as_identity(given, out, expected)? } else { self.expr(given, out)? };
                if !ty.assignable_to(expected) { return Err(type_error(given.site(), format!("{name} requires {}, got {}", expected.name(), ty.name()), "pass the query's declared argument type")); }
                fields.insert(name.clone(), value);
            }
            let cursors: Vec<_> = query.args.iter().filter(|(_, ty)| ty.required() == Ty::Cursor).map(|(name, _)| name.clone()).collect();
            let cursor = (cursors.len() == 1).then(|| cursors[0].clone());
            let ty = if all {
                let Some((item, _)) = query.result.sequence() else { return Err(diagnostic(site, "E_JOB_VIEWER_QUERY", "all needs a query returning a row list", "return the paged list from the query")); };
                if cursor.is_none() || snapback4_core::engine::drain_cursor(&query.program) != cursor { return Err(diagnostic(site, "E_JOB_VIEWER_QUERY", "all needs one cursor argument that owns the returned page", "declare c: cursor ? and return a page after c; start with null")); }
                Ty::List(Box::new(item), u32::MAX)
            } else { Ty::Object(BTreeMap::from([("data".into(), query.result), ("next".into(), Ty::Cursor.optional())])) };
            Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::JobQuery { program: Box::new(query.program), cursor, all }, args: vec![Expr::Object(fields)] }, ty))
        })())
    }

    fn collision_lookup(&mut self, table: &str, name: &str, index: &crate::schema::Index, key: &[Value], except: Option<&str>, effect: Effect) -> Result<Option<Value>, RuntimeError> {
        let probes = super::rules::rule_probes(&self.schema.tables[table].rules.read);

            let found = if runner.schema.tables[table].not_before.is_some() {

                runner.live_lookup(allowance, table, name, index, key, #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")] None)?

                runner.visible_collision(table, row, effect, &format!("unique {}", index.columns().join(", ")))?;
            }
            Ok(found)
        })
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — hidden collisions use the ordinary write-rule refusal
    fn visible_collision(
        &mut self,
        table: &str,
        row: &Value,
        effect: Effect,
        clause: &str,
    ) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let mut image = row.clone();
        let definition = self.schema.table(table).expect("validated");
        materialize_optional_fields(&mut image, definition);
        if self.inactive_write_target(table, &image)? || !self.check_rule(table, Effect::Read, None, &image)? {
            return Err(self.rule_refusal(table, effect, clause));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// `after insert <- exists t[...]` holds for every row inserted this
    /// transaction; checked once the program has run.
    pub(super) fn check_final_exists(&mut self) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let inserted = std::mem::take(&mut self.inserted);
        for (table_name, row) in &inserted {
            let table = self.schema.table(table_name).expect("validated");
            for constraint in &table.constraints {
                let Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { table: target, index, key } = constraint else { continue;
                };
                let refusal = || {
                    RuntimeError::Constraint(format!("inserting into {table_name} requires a matching row in {target} by the end of the mutation"))
                };
                let has_references = key.iter().any(|term| term.reference_source().is_some());
                let key: Vec<Value> = if has_references {
                    // Preserve the structural target probe, but authorize each
                    // live row supplying its key before it can confer authority.
                    let rule = crate::schema::RuleExpr::Exists { table: target.clone(), index: index.clone(), key: key.clone(), equalities: vec![], provenance: crate::ir::KeyProvenance::Shape };
                    for term in key { if let crate::schema::RuleTerm::Field(field) = term { self.provisional_sequence_read |= self.device && table.sequences.contains_key(field); } }
                    self.final_reference_key(table_name, &rule, row)?.ok_or_else(refusal)?
                } else { key
                    .iter()
                    .map(|term| match term {
                        crate::schema::RuleTerm::Field(field) | crate::schema::RuleTerm::NextField(field) => {
                            // This inserted image owns a provisional ordinal even if no expression read it.
                            self.provisional_sequence_read |= self.device && table.sequences.contains_key(field);
                            row.field(field).cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null)
                        }
                            crate::schema::RuleTerm::Viewer => {
                                Value::Id(self.context.viewer.clone())
                            }
                            crate::schema::RuleTerm::Literal(value) => value.clone(),
                        crate::schema::RuleTerm::OldField(_) | crate::schema::RuleTerm::Reference { .. } | crate::schema::RuleTerm::ReferenceChain { .. } => Value::Null,
                    })
                    .collect() };
                self.read_tables.insert(target.clone());
                self.observe_sequence_selection(target, index, &key)?;
                let definition = self.schema.table(target).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing {target}")))?;
                let target_index = definition.index(index).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing {target}.{index}")))?;
                let found = match self.lookup_stored(target, index, target_index, &key, true)? {
                    Some(row) => self.live_aggregate(target, row)?,
                refusal.rewrite = Some("drop this binding's debt; collect and report using the current binding fingerprint".into());
                refusal.guide = Some("receipts".into());
            }
            #[cfg(feature = "server-search")]
            Self::SearchOpening { site, rewrite, .. } => {
                refusal.site = Some(site.clone());
                refusal.rewrite = rewrite.clone();
                refusal.guide = Some("search".into());
            }
            Self::NamedConstraint { code, message, detail } => {
                refusal.rule = Some(code.clone());
                refusal.message = message.clone();
                refusal.detail = Some(detail.clone());
                refusal.guide = Some("indexes".into());
            }
            Self::Require { code, site, message } => {
                refusal.rule = Some(code.clone());
                refusal.site = site.clone();
                refusal.message = message.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| format!("the program refused with {code}"));
                refusal.guide = Some("programs".into());
            }
            #[cfg(not(all(target_arch = "wasm32", feature = "web", not(feature = "sqlite"))))]
            Self::Structural { code: "E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT", message } => {
                refusal.message = message.clone();
                refusal.rewrite = Some("iterate the original capped group, read the page in a query, or use a job sweep; `snapback4 check` locates the source and names the bound".into());
                refusal.guide = Some("programs".into());
            }
