    fn scan(&mut self, read: &ReadExpr, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<(Scan, u32)> {
        self.scan_at(read, out, prefix::Position::Page)
    }

    fn scan_at(&mut self, read: &ReadExpr, out: &mut setup::Body, position: prefix::Position) -> Fallible<(Scan, u32)> {
        let info = self.table(&read.table, &read.site)?;
        let (keys, index, selection) = self.select_index(info, read, ReadMode::Range, out)?;
        let prefix = self.order_keys(info, &index, keys)?;
        // @ref LLP 3000.014#5.1 — one pinned parent authorizes all of its aggregate groups.
        if let Some(m) = self.schema.maintain_for(&read.table).filter(|m| m.groups_by_parent(self.schema)) {
            let parent = self.schema.tables[&m.source].through.as_ref().unwrap();
            if m.parent_key.is_none() || !index.columns.iter().take(prefix.len()).any(|f| f == &parent.reference) {
                let fields = m.by.iter().filter(|f| *f != &parent.reference).map(|f| format!(".{f}")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
                let order = if fields.is_empty() { ".id" } else { &fields };
                return Err(Diagnostic::new(&read.site, "E_READ_THROUGH_SCAN",
                    format!("{} must pin {} to one readable {} row before enumerating groups", read.table, parent.reference, parent.parent),
                    format!("inside a page of {}, read `{}[{} = .id] by {order}` in its shape: `{{ *, totals: {}[{} = .id] by {order} }}`; keep the parent page's audience key, order and cursor. For a scalar supply every group key: {}[{}]. Omit an explicit aggregate read rule to inherit parent authorization", parent.parent, read.table, parent.reference, read.table, parent.reference, read.table, m.by.join(", "))).guide("maintains"));
            }
        }
        let (range, bound) = self.prefix_bound(read, &index, position)?;
        if info.maintained.is_some() && let Some(position) = index.columns.iter().position(|field| field == "value") {
            if prefix.len() != position {
                return Err(super::maintains::refusal(&range.site, format!("{} by {} needs every ranking scope field pinned: {}", read.table, index.name, index.columns[..position].join(", ")),
                    format!("pin {} with where equalities, then read {} last {} by .value after c; omit the scope predicate for a global ranking", index.columns[..position].join(", "), read.table, range.take)));
            }
        }
        if range.take == 0 {
            return Err(type_error(&range.site, "a page holds at least one row", print::read_expr(&ReadExpr { range: Some(ast::RangeSpec { take: 50, ..range.clone() }), ..read.clone() })));
        }
        let mut page_source = read.clone();
        page_source.computed.extend(index.computed.iter().map(|(key, value)| {
            let mut value = value.clone();
            if let A::Call { args, .. } = &mut value
                && let Some(A::Name { name, site }) = args.first().cloned() {
                args[0] = A::Member { base: Box::new(A::Focal { site: site.clone() }), name, site };
            }
            (key.clone(), value)
        }));
        for (key, column) in page_source.keys.iter_mut().zip(&index.columns) {
            key.column.get_or_insert_with(|| column.clone());
        }
        let filter_text = read.filter.as_ref().map(|expr| self.catalog.source.expression(expr));
        let (read, filter) = self.scan_filter(read, &index)?;
        let read = &read;
        // Key expressions precede the seek bounds and cursor, including their setup.
        let prefix: Vec<Expr> = prefix.into_iter().map(|value| self.snapshot(value, out)).collect();
        let seek = self.seek(info, read, &index, out)?;
        let mut after = None;
        if let Some(cursor) = &range.cursor {
            let (e, t) = self.expr(cursor, out)?;
            if !matches!(t.required(), Ty::Cursor) {
                return Err(type_error(cursor.site(), format!("after expects a cursor, got {}", t.name()), "declare c: cursor ? and pass after c"));
            }
            if !info.total_cursor(&index) {
                let columns = index.columns.iter().map(|column| index.computed.get(column)
                    .map(print::expression).unwrap_or_else(|| column.clone())).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
                if index.unique {
                    // Do not add id to the unique constraint: that would
                    // weaken it. Plan a separate pageable index from the read.
                    let mut planned = read.clone();
                    let rewrite = if index.computed.is_empty() {
                        planned.index = None;
                        for (key, column) in planned.keys.iter_mut().zip(&index.columns) { key.column.get_or_insert_with(|| column.clone()); }
                        planned.order_keys = index.columns.iter().skip(prefix.len()).cloned().collect();
                        print::read_expr(&planned)
                    } else {
                        let mut name = format!("{}Page", index.name);
                        while info.indexes.iter().any(|index| index.name == name) { name.push('_'); }
                        planned.index = Some(name.clone());
                        format!("add `by {name}: {columns}, id` to {}; read `{}`", read.table, print::read_expr(&planned))
                    };
                    return Err(Diagnostic::new(&range.site, "E_CURSOR_INDEX", format!("index {}.{} cannot carry a cursor: its nullable unique key allows tied null rows without an id tiebreak", read.table, index.name), rewrite).guide("indexes"));
                }
                return Err(Diagnostic::new(&range.site, "E_CURSOR_INDEX", format!("index {}.{} cannot carry a cursor: it has no declared id or total unique key", read.table, index.name), format!("by {}: {columns}, id", index.name)).guide("indexes").mechanical());
        if let Some(matching) = &read.matching {
            // The search text follows the keys as the word term; the index
            // was chosen for its words component in exactly that position.
            let (e, t) = self.expr(matching, out)?;
            if !matches!(t, Ty::Text(_)) {
                let rewrite = if matches!(t, Ty::Optional(ref inner) if matches!(**inner, Ty::Text(_))) { format!("{} ?? ''", print::expression(matching)) } else { "matching q  -- with q: text <=100".to_owned() };
                return Err(type_error(matching.site(), format!("matching takes present text, got {}", t.name()), rewrite));
            }
            prefix.push(IndexKeyExpr::WordPrefix(e));
        }
        let scan_site = self.site();
        self.page_sources.insert(scan_site.clone(), page_source);
        let pins = read.keys.iter().enumerate().map(|(position, key)| {
            let column = key.column.as_ref().unwrap_or(&index.columns[position]);
            format!(".{column} = {}", self.catalog.source.operand(&key.value))
        }).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" and ");
        let domain = if pins.is_empty() { read.table.clone() } else { format!("{} where {pins}", read.table) };
        self.sources.insert(format!("domain/{scan_site}"), (read.site.clone(), domain));
        if filter.is_some() && let Some(text) = filter_text { self.filters.insert(scan_site.clone(), text); }
        // Only the generated scan itself, never an authored scan bound inside its keys, cursor or helpers.
        if self.expanding_feed.as_ref().is_some_and(|(feed, site)| *feed == read.table && *site == read.site) { self.timeline_scans.insert(scan_site.clone()); }
        self.record_selection(&scan_site, read, &index, if position == prefix::Position::Exists { "exists" } else { "page" }, &selection);
        // Authored spelling serves diagnostics; inferred-index residency sites
        // keep canonical bytes. Explicit-index search alternatives retain their
        // authored origin even when presence planning synthesizes a browse index.
        if !read.order_keys.is_empty() && let Some(text) = self.catalog.canonical_read_origins.get(&read.site.to_string()) {
            self.canonical_sources.insert(scan_site.clone(), text.clone());
        }
        let spelling = if !read.order_keys.is_empty() { self.catalog.read_origins.get(&read.site.to_string()).cloned() } else { None };
        self.sources.insert(scan_site.clone(), (read.site.clone(), spelling.unwrap_or_else(|| print::read_expr(&ReadExpr { index: None, range: None, matching: None, filter: None, seeks: Vec::new(), ..read.clone() }))));
        let mut scan = Scan { cursor_pins: read.cursor_prefix.map_or(0, |old| (read.keys.len() - old) as u32),
            variant: self.variant(),
            site: scan_site,
            table: read.table.clone(),
            index: index.name,

//! The three diary shapes, using the current producers and their JSON envelope.
use snapback4_lang::{Bound, Diagnostic, bind::residency};

const REFERENCE: &str = "table posts:\n  body: text <=100\n  public 'posts'\n  insert <- allow\ntable events:\n  postId: posts\n  public 'feed events'\nfn deliver(event: events): event\nmutation publish():\n  post = insert posts {body: 'hello'}\n  return deliver(post)\n";
const MEMBERSHIP: &str = "table conversations:\n  public 'test'\ntable members:\n  conversationId: conversations\n  principal: principal\n  unique byConversationPrincipal: conversationId, principal\n  read <- .principal = viewer\ntable reactions:\n  conversationId: conversations\n  messageId: id\n  by byMessage: messageId, id\n  by byConversationMessage: conversationId, messageId, id\n  read <- exists members[.conversationId, viewer]\nquery reactionsForMessage(conversationId: conversations, messageId: id):\n  return reactions[messageId] first 20 by byMessage\n";
const PRESENCE: &str = "effect notify\ntable notes:\n  n: int\n  unique byN: n\n  public 'notes'\n  sync public\n  insert <- allow\nmutation send(p: principal):\n  insert notes {n: 1}\n  if not exists connected[p]:\n    emit notify {row: notes[n = 1]}\n";

fn compile(source: &str) -> Bound { snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]) }
fn clean(source: &str) -> Bound {
    let b = compile(source); assert!(b.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", b.diagnostics); b
}
fn report(name: &str, diagnostics: &[Diagnostic]) {
    for diagnostic in diagnostics { println!("{name} terminal:\n{diagnostic}"); }
    println!("{name} JSON: {}", serde_json::to_string(diagnostics).unwrap());
}

#[test]
fn capture_existing_three_builder_cases() {
    let reference = compile(REFERENCE);
    report("reference", &reference.diagnostics);
    let control = include_str!("fixtures/builder-guidance-control.txt");
    assert!(control.contains(&reference.diagnostics[0].to_string()), "the already sufficient helper explanation stays unchanged");
    assert!(control.contains(&format!("reference JSON: {}", serde_json::to_string(&reference.diagnostics).unwrap())));
    assert_eq!(reference.diagnostics.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(reference.diagnostics[0].code, "E_QUARRY_TYPE");
    assert!(reference.diagnostics[0].message.contains("deliver's event"));
    assert!(!reference.diagnostics[0].mechanical);
    let membership = clean(MEMBERSHIP);
    let notes: Vec<_> = membership.notes.iter().filter(|note| note.code == "N_NEVER_COMPLETE").cloned().collect();
    report("membership", &notes); assert_eq!(notes.len(), 1);
    assert!(notes[0].message.contains(".conversationId, which the scan does not pin"));
    assert!(!notes[0].mechanical);
    let presence = clean(PRESENCE);
    let fact = &presence.schema.operations["send"];
    println!("presence why:\n{}", residency::operation_lines("send", fact));
    println!("presence JSON: {}", serde_json::to_string(fact).unwrap());
    assert_eq!(fact.predicts.as_deref(), Some("eligible"));
    assert!(fact.connected_effects_only);
    assert!(fact.effect_payload_reads.iter().any(|site| site.reason.contains("server-only, feeds an effect") && site.site == "schema.q:11:23 (notes[n = 1])"));
}

#[test]
fn scope_guidance_uses_existing_index_and_preserves_the_message_equality() {
    let b = clean(MEMBERSHIP);
    let note = b.notes.iter().find(|note| note.code == "N_NEVER_COMPLETE").unwrap();
    assert!(note.rewrite.contains("existing index `byConversationMessage: conversationId, messageId, id`"), "{note}");
    assert!(note.rewrite.contains("current equality prefix"));
    assert!(note.rewrite.contains("narrows the answer"));
    assert!(!note.rewrite.contains("by byConversationId"));
    assert!(!note.mechanical);
    let json = serde_json::to_value(note).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(json["rewrite"], note.rewrite); assert_eq!(json["mechanical"], false);

    let without_index = MEMBERSHIP.replace("  by byConversationMessage: conversationId, messageId, id\n", "");
    let b = clean(&without_index);
    let note = b.notes.iter().find(|note| note.code == "N_NEVER_COMPLETE").unwrap();
    assert!(note.rewrite.contains("pin .conversationId with where equalities"), "{note}");
    let rewritten = without_index.replace("reactions[messageId] first 20 by byMessage", "reactions where .conversationId = conversationId and .messageId = messageId first 20 by .id");
    assert!(!clean(&rewritten).notes.iter().any(|note| note.code == "N_NEVER_COMPLETE"));

    let incompatible = MEMBERSHIP.replace("by byConversationMessage: conversationId, messageId, id", "by byConversationMessage: conversationId, id, messageId");
    let b = clean(&incompatible);
    assert!(!b.notes.iter().find(|note| note.code == "N_NEVER_COMPLETE").unwrap().rewrite.contains("existing index"), "do not change the unpinned ordering");
}

#[test]
fn presence_guidance_connects_the_existing_origin_to_the_consuming_read() {
    // A shared read still costs prediction; the effect-only case below no
    // longer needs the old hoisting workaround.
    let shared = PRESENCE.replace("    emit notify {row: notes[n = 1]}", "    row = notes[n = 1]\n    if row != null:\n      emit notify {row}");
    let b = clean(&shared); let fact = &b.schema.operations["send"];
    let blocked: Vec<_> = fact.sites.iter().filter(|site| site.kind == "presence").collect();
    assert!(blocked.len() >= 2, "retain the presence causes");
    let read = blocked.iter().find(|site| site.reason.contains("a fallible evaluation")).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(read.site, "schema.q:11:11 (notes[n = 1])");
    assert!(read.reason.contains("connected[p]") && read.reason.contains("schema.q:10:17"));
    assert_eq!(fact.predicts.as_deref(), Some("never"));
    assert!(residency::operation_lines("send", fact).contains("fallible evaluation (read at schema.q:10:17) (site schema.q:11:11 (notes[n = 1]))"));
    assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(read).unwrap()["site"], read.site);
    let hoisted = PRESENCE.replace("  if not exists connected[p]:\n    emit notify {row: notes[n = 1]}", "  row = notes[n = 1]\n  if not exists connected[p]:\n    emit notify {row}");
    let previous = clean(&hoisted);
    let notes = residency::change_notes(&b, &previous.schema.operations);
    assert_eq!(notes.len(), 1, "one existing prediction-loss note");
    assert_eq!(notes[0].code, "N_NOT_PREDICTABLE");
    assert!(!notes[0].mechanical);
    assert!(notes[0].message.contains("schema.q:11:11"));
    let effect_only = clean(PRESENCE);
    assert_eq!(effect_only.schema.operations["send"].predicts.as_deref(), Some("eligible"));
    assert!(residency::operation_lines("send", &effect_only.schema.operations["send"]).contains("server-only, feeds an effect"));
}

#[test]
fn same_table_row_helpers_and_explicit_author_choices_still_compile() {
    let same_table = REFERENCE.replace("event: events", "event: posts");
    clean(&same_table); // Same-table row-to-reference behavior is intentional.
    let corrected = MEMBERSHIP.replace("reactions[messageId] first 20 by byMessage", "reactions[conversationId, messageId] first 20 by byConversationMessage");
    let b = clean(&corrected); assert!(!b.notes.iter().any(|note| note.code == "N_NEVER_COMPLETE"));
    // This author-selected rewrite changes when the read runs. It is not an
    // automatic repair: evaluating it unconditionally can introduce refusal.
    let hoisted = PRESENCE.replace("  if not exists connected[p]:\n    emit notify {row: notes[n = 1]}", "  row = notes[n = 1]\n  if not exists connected[p]:\n    emit notify {row}");
    assert_eq!(clean(&hoisted).schema.operations["send"].predicts.as_deref(), Some("eligible"));
}

//! A table-typed argument is an id with a stronger name. Storing it in a
//! reference column still does not prove that the target row exists.

use super::catalog::Catalog;
use crate::{
    ast::{Expr, FunctionBody, ProgramKind, ReadExpr, Stmt, TypeKind, WriteOp},
    diag::{Diagnostic, Site},
};
use snapback4_core::schema::{Constraint, RuleExpr, RuleTerm, Schema};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

#[derive(Clone)]
struct Candidate {
    argument: String,
    target: String,
    child: String,
    column: String,
    op: WriteOp,
    site: Site,
    checked: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
struct Flow {
    /// Arguments whose name still denotes the mutation input, rather than a
    /// later binding with the same spelling.
    inputs: BTreeSet<String>,
    checked: BTreeSet<String>,
}

/// Name a likely missing existence check. Known helpers count only when their
/// body actually looks up the argument; passing an id through does not.
// @ref LLP 3000.039#7 — reference types validate id shape, never target
// existence; `N_REFERENCE_UNCHECKED` points to the explicit lookup form.
pub(super) fn notes(catalog: &Catalog, schema: &Schema) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
    let mut notes = Vec::new();
    for doc in &catalog.documents {
        for program in doc
            .programs
            .iter()
            .filter(|program| program.kind == ProgramKind::Mutation && !program.native)
        {
            let arguments: BTreeMap<String, String> = program
                .args
                .iter()
                .filter_map(|arg| match &arg.type_.kind {
                    TypeKind::Ref { table } => Some((arg.name.clone(), table.clone())),
                    _ => None,
                })
                .collect();
            if arguments.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }

            let mut candidates = Vec::new();
            let flow = Flow {
                inputs: arguments.keys().cloned().collect(),
                checked: BTreeSet::new(),
            };
            let body: Vec<_> = program
                .prelude
                .iter()
                .chain(&program.body)
                .cloned()
                .collect();
            flow_statements(catalog, schema, &arguments, &body, flow, &mut candidates);

            let mut emitted = BTreeSet::new();
            for candidate in candidates {
                if candidate.checked
                    || write_contract_checks(schema, &candidate)
                    || !emitted.insert(candidate.argument.clone())
                {
                    continue;
                }
                notes.push(Diagnostic::new(&candidate.site, "N_REFERENCE_UNCHECKED",
                    format!("mutation {} stores argument {} directly in {}.{}, but never looks up {}[{}]: a reference accepts any well-formed id even when the row is absent", program.name, candidate.argument, candidate.child, candidate.column, candidate.target, candidate.argument),
                    format!("bind `parent = {}[{}] ! else NOT_FOUND` before the write, then store `parent.id`; keep the direct id only when dangling references are intentional", candidate.target, candidate.argument)).guide("types"));
            }
        }
    }
    notes
}

/// Follow only paths that can reach a write. A lookup fact joins by
/// intersection, so one conditional arm, a short-circuited operand, or a
/// possibly-empty loop can never authorize a later candidate.
fn flow_statements(
    catalog: &Catalog,
    schema: &Schema,
    arguments: &BTreeMap<String, String>,
    body: &[Stmt],
    mut flow: Flow,
    candidates: &mut Vec<Candidate>,
) -> Option<Flow> {
    for statement in body {
        match statement {
            Stmt::Bind { names, value, .. } => {
                flow_expression(catalog, schema, arguments, value, &mut flow, candidates);
                for name in names {
                    flow.inputs.remove(name);
                    flow.checked.remove(name);
                }
            }
            Stmt::Expr { value, .. } => {
                flow_expression(catalog, schema, arguments, value, &mut flow, candidates)
            }
            Stmt::Require { condition, .. } => {
                let (admitted, _) =
                    flow_condition(catalog, schema, arguments, condition, flow, candidates);
                flow = admitted;
            }
            Stmt::Return { value, .. } => {
                flow_expression(catalog, schema, arguments, value, &mut flow, candidates);
                return None;
            }
            Stmt::Emit { payload, once, .. } => {
                flow_expression(catalog, schema, arguments, payload, &mut flow, candidates);
                if let Some(once) = once {
                    flow_expression(catalog, schema, arguments, once, &mut flow, candidates);
                }
            }
            Stmt::If {
                condition,
                then_body,
                else_body,
                ..
            } => {
                let (then_entry, else_entry) =
                    flow_condition(catalog, schema, arguments, condition, flow, candidates);
                let then_flow = flow_statements(
                    catalog,
                    schema,
                    arguments,
                    then_body,
                    then_entry,
                    candidates,
                );
                let else_flow = flow_statements(
                    catalog,
                    schema,
                    arguments,
                    else_body,
                    else_entry,
                    candidates,
                );
                flow = join_flows(then_flow, else_flow)?;
            }
            Stmt::For {
                name, domain, body, ..
            } => {
                flow_expression(catalog, schema, arguments, domain, &mut flow, candidates);
                let mut iteration = flow.clone();
                iteration.inputs.remove(name);
                iteration.checked.remove(name);
                let _ = flow_statements(catalog, schema, arguments, body, iteration, candidates);
                // The domain may be empty, so body facts are never carried out.
            }
            Stmt::As {
                principal, body, ..
            } => {
                flow_expression(catalog, schema, arguments, principal, &mut flow, candidates);
                flow = flow_statements(catalog, schema, arguments, body, flow, candidates)?;
            }
            Stmt::Break { .. } | Stmt::Continue { .. } => return None,
        }
    }
    Some(flow)
}

fn join_flows(left: Option<Flow>, right: Option<Flow>) -> Option<Flow> {
    match (left, right) {
        (Some(mut left), Some(right)) => {
            left.inputs.retain(|name| right.inputs.contains(name));
            left.checked.retain(|name| right.checked.contains(name));
            Some(left)
        }
        (Some(flow), None) | (None, Some(flow)) => Some(flow),
        (None, None) => None,
    }
}

fn flow_expression(
    catalog: &Catalog,
    schema: &Schema,
    arguments: &BTreeMap<String, String>,
    expression: &Expr,
    flow: &mut Flow,
    candidates: &mut Vec<Candidate>,
) {
    let child = |value: &Expr, flow: &mut Flow, candidates: &mut Vec<Candidate>| {
        flow_expression(catalog, schema, arguments, value, flow, candidates)
    };
    match expression {
        Expr::Read(read) | Expr::Exists { read, .. } => {
            flow_read(catalog, schema, arguments, read, flow, candidates);
            for (name, target) in arguments {
                if flow.inputs.contains(name)
                    && target == &read.table
                    && read_checks_target_id(schema, read, name, target)
                {
                    flow.checked.insert(name.clone());
                }
            }
        }
        Expr::Created { read, .. } => flow_read(catalog, schema, arguments, read, flow, candidates),
        Expr::Unary { value, .. }
        | Expr::Member { base: value, .. }
        | Expr::Assert { value, .. }
        | Expr::ShapeUse { base: value, .. }
        | Expr::Walk { seed: value, .. } => child(value, flow, candidates),
        Expr::Binary { op, left, right, .. }
            if matches!(op.as_str(), "and" | "or" | "??") => {
            child(left, flow, candidates);
            if lazy_right_must_run(op, left) {
                child(right, flow, candidates);
            } else {
                flow_conditional_expression(catalog, schema, arguments, right, flow, candidates);
            }
        }
            if let Some(value) = &merge.matching {
                child(value, flow, candidates);
            }
            if let Some(value) = &merge.filter {
                flow_conditional_expression(catalog, schema, arguments, value, flow, candidates);
            }
            if let Some(value) = &merge.cursor {
                child(value, flow, candidates);
            }
            for lane in &merge.lanes {
                for value in &lane.prefix {
                    child(value, flow, candidates);
                }
                if let Some(value) = &lane.distinct {
                    flow_conditional_expression(catalog, schema, arguments, value, flow, candidates);
                }
                if let Some((_, value)) = &lane.loop_ {
                    child(value, flow, candidates);
                }
                if let Some(value) = &lane.admission {
                    flow_conditional_expression(catalog, schema, arguments, value, flow, candidates);
                }
                if let Some(fields) = &lane.project {
                    for field in fields {
                        if let crate::ast::ShapeField::Field { value, .. } = field {
                            flow_conditional_expression(catalog, schema, arguments, value, flow, candidates);
                        }
                    }
                }
                if let Some(read) = &lane.planned {
                    flow_conditional_read(catalog, schema, arguments, read, flow, candidates);
                }
                if let Some((_, read)) = &lane.nulls {
                    flow_conditional_read(catalog, schema, arguments, read, flow, candidates);
                }
            }
        }
        Expr::Name { .. } | Expr::Focal { .. } | Expr::Literal { .. } => {}
    }
}

/// Facts on boolean edges. This preserves the useful distinction between
/// `require ready and checked(parent)` (the check is mandatory on the true
/// edge) and `require ready or checked(parent)` (it can still be skipped).
fn flow_condition(
    catalog: &Catalog,
    schema: &Schema,
    arguments: &BTreeMap<String, String>,
    expression: &Expr,
    flow: Flow,
    candidates: &mut Vec<Candidate>,
) -> (Flow, Flow) {
    match expression {
        Expr::Unary { op, value, .. } if op == "not" => {
            let (yes, no) =
                flow_condition(catalog, schema, arguments, value, flow, candidates);
            (no, yes)
        }
        Expr::Binary {
            op, left, right, ..
        } if op == "and" => {
            let (left_yes, left_no) =
                flow_condition(catalog, schema, arguments, left, flow, candidates);
            let (right_yes, right_no) =
                flow_condition(catalog, schema, arguments, right, left_yes, candidates);
            (
                right_yes,
                join_flows(Some(left_no), Some(right_no)).unwrap(),
            )
        }
        Expr::Binary {
            op, left, right, ..
        } if op == "or" => {
            let (left_yes, left_no) =
                flow_condition(catalog, schema, arguments, left, flow, candidates);
            let (right_yes, right_no) =
                flow_condition(catalog, schema, arguments, right, left_no, candidates);
            (
                join_flows(Some(left_yes), Some(right_yes)).unwrap(),
                right_no,
            )
        }
        // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#7 — storing null needs no target lookup;
        // intersect that edge with the checked non-null edge after the if.
        Expr::Binary { op, left, right, .. } if op == "=" || op == "!=" => {
            let mut evaluated = flow;
            flow_expression(catalog, schema, arguments, expression, &mut evaluated, candidates);
            let mut yes = evaluated.clone();
            let mut no = evaluated;
            let name = match (left.as_ref(), right.as_ref()) {
                (Expr::Name { name, .. }, Expr::Literal { value: crate::ast::Literal::Null, .. })
                | (Expr::Literal { value: crate::ast::Literal::Null, .. }, Expr::Name { name, .. }) => Some(name),
                _ => None,
            };
            if let Some(name) = name.filter(|name| yes.inputs.contains(*name)) {
                if op == "=" { yes.checked.insert(name.clone()); }
                else { no.checked.insert(name.clone()); }
            }
            (yes, no)
        }
        _ => {
            let mut evaluated = flow;
            flow_expression(
                catalog,
                schema,
                arguments,
                expression,
                &mut evaluated,
                candidates,
            );
            (evaluated.clone(), evaluated)
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn w9c_emit_only_bounded_lists_record_effects_on_server() {
    for (name, body, count) in LOOPS {
        let bound = compile(&loop_source(body));
        let mut engine = Engine::memory(bound.schema.clone(), bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap();
        engine.seed([("batches".into(), snapback4_core::wire::row_from_json(&bound.schema.tables["batches"], &json!({"id":"batch", "recipients":["bob","carol"], "numbers":[1,2,3]})).unwrap())].into_iter().chain(
            ["alice", "bob", "carol"].map(|p| ("members".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id(p)), ("principal", id(p))]))))).unwrap();
        let result = engine.mutate("send", Some("send"), Context::new("alice", args(&[("batchId", id("batch"))])).at(100)).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(result.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{name}: {result:?}");
        let effects = engine.effects(None, 10).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(effects.len(), *count, "{name}");
        let mut recipients: Vec<_> = effects.iter().map(|e| e.payload.field("recipient").unwrap().clone()).collect();
        recipients.sort_by_key(|v| snapback4_core::wire::to_json(v).to_string());
        assert_eq!(recipients, if *name == "scalar_column" { vec![Value::Int(1), Value::Int(2), Value::Int(3)] } else { vec![id("bob"), id("carol")] }, "{name}");
        assert_eq!(result.metered.rows_written, 0);
        // The same id must replay with the same arguments: a differing input is
        // now a terminal id-reuse refusal, not a replay.
        assert!(engine.mutate("send", Some("send"), Context::new("alice", args(&[("batchId", id("batch"))])).at(100)).unwrap().replayed);
        assert_eq!(engine.effects(None, 10).unwrap(), effects);
        println!("server {name}: {count} emissions, 0 rows written, replay adds 0 emissions");
    }
}

#[test]
fn w9c_unique_hook_and_legacy_refusals_on_server() {
    for (hook, code, message) in [
        (" else HANDLE_TAKEN 'That handle is taken.'", "HANDLE_TAKEN", "That handle is taken."),
        (" else HANDLE_TAKEN", "HANDLE_TAKEN", "the program refused with HANDLE_TAKEN"),
        ("", "E_CONSTRAINT", "profiles.byHandle already has a row where handle = 'alice'"),
    ] {
        let bound = compile(&profiles(hook));
        let mut engine = Engine::memory(bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap();
        let create = |engine: &mut Engine, key: &str, handle: &str| engine.mutate("create", Some(key), Context::new("alice", args(&[("handle", Value::String(handle.into()))])).with_ids([key.into()])).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(create(&mut engine, "p1", "alice").state, WriteState::Sent { .. }));
        let duplicate = create(&mut engine, "p2", "alice");
        let WriteState::Failed { why, .. } = duplicate.state else { panic!("{duplicate:?}") };
        assert_eq!((why.code.as_str(), why.message.as_str()), (code, message));
        if !hook.is_empty() { assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(&why).unwrap()["detail"], "profiles.byHandle already has a row where handle = 'alice'"); }
        println!("server refusal: {why}");
        assert_eq!(engine.store().count("profiles").unwrap(), 1);
        assert!(matches!(create(&mut engine, "p3", "bob").state, WriteState::Sent { .. }));
        let rename = engine.mutate("rename", Some("rename"), Context::new("alice", args(&[("profile", id("p3")), ("handle", Value::String("alice".into()))]))).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(rename.state, WriteState::Failed { ref why, .. } if why.code == code));
        let absent = engine.mutate("tryCreate", Some("try"), Context::new("alice", args(&[("handle", Value::String("alice".into()))])).with_ids(["p4".into()])).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(absent.state, WriteState::Sent { result: Value::Null, .. }));
    }
}

#[test]
fn w9c_unique_hook_preserves_hidden_collision_refusal() {
    let source = profiles(" else HANDLE_TAKEN 'That handle is taken.'").replace("  public 'profiles'", "  owner: principal default viewer\n  read <- .owner = viewer").replace("  sync\n", "  by byOwner: owner, id\n  sync to .owner\n");
    let bound = compile(&source);
    // The metadata survives the wire/storage schema form.
    let schema = serde_json::from_value(serde_json::to_value(&bound.schema).unwrap()).unwrap();
    let mut engine = Engine::memory(schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap();
    let create = |engine: &mut Engine, viewer: &str, key: &str| engine.mutate("create", Some(key), Context::new(viewer, args(&[("handle", Value::String("alice".into()))])).with_ids([key.into()])).unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(create(&mut engine, "alice", "p1").state, WriteState::Sent { .. }));
    let hidden = create(&mut engine, "bob", "p2");
    let WriteState::Failed { why, .. } = hidden.state else { panic!("{hidden:?}") };
    assert_eq!(why.code, "E_RULE");
    assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(&why).unwrap().get("detail"), None);
    assert!(!why.message.contains("byHandle"));
    assert_eq!(engine.store().count("profiles").unwrap(), 1);
}

use super::catalog::{Catalog, TableInfo};

pub(super) fn candidates<'a>(info: &'a TableInfo, read: &ReadExpr, types: &[(Ty, bool)], synthesized: &std::collections::BTreeSet<(String, String)>) -> Vec<&'a IndexDecl> {
    let identity = read.index.is_none() && types.len() == 1 &&
        (types[0].0.required() == Ty::Id || types[0].0.required() == Ty::Ref(read.table.clone()));
    info.indexes.iter().filter(|index| !synthesized.contains(&(read.table.clone(), index.name.clone())))
        .filter(|index| match &read.index {
            Some(name) => &index.name == name,
            None if identity => index.name == "byId",
            None => index.unique && index.columns.len() == types.len(),
        })
        // Explicit indexes keep their existing mismatch diagnostics and range semantics.
        .filter(|index| read.index.is_some() || types.iter().zip(&index.columns).all(|((ty, literal), column)| {
            let expected = if index.computed.contains_key(column) { Ty::Int }
                else if column == "id" { Ty::Ref(read.table.clone()) }
                else { info.columns.get(column).map(Ty::from_scalar).unwrap_or(Ty::Unknown) };
            ty.comparable(&expected) || (*literal && expected.is_identity())
        })).collect()
}

+## 7. Wave 11 diagnostic precision (QDIAG)
+
+The nullable-reference lint counts a null value as needing no target lookup.
+At `if arg != null`, only the null edge carries that exemption; a lookup on
+the other edge must still dominate the write. Join by intersection and clear
+facts on rebinding. This changes advisory output only.
+
+Operation parameter defaults remain explicit: declare an optional parameter
+and bind `value = arg ?? literal`. Refuse `= literal` with that exact idiom.
+A multi-line `require` keeps `else CODE` on its closing line; the refusal names
+that line and preserves the author's code. `?` precedes `on delete keep`.
+
+## 8. Wave 11 contextual spellings and refusal codes (QDIAG amendment)
+
+A required same-table row in a reference-typed column, point key, or operation
+argument lowers to its `.id`. This includes an inserted snapshot and a looked-up
+snapshot; it evaluates its expression once in source order, introduces no
+lookup, and grants no existence or read authority. Shorthand fields get the same
+projection. Cross-table rows and optional rows remain refused; an optional
+upsert must be narrowed with `! else CODE` first. A generic `id` or `principal`
+position does not implicitly project a row. Helper parameters retain their
+existing call-site row specialization (LLP 3000.007 §18.5): a helper called with
+a row keeps its row fields, and one called with a reference must look it up.
+Lists and objects receive no deep automatic projection. Explicit `.id` remains
+valid. Generated API and runtime IR remain those of the explicit spelling.
+
+Image and video bounds accept integer decimal byte units KB, MB and GB; 5MB
+means 5,000,000 bytes. Overflow above u32 refuses at parsing. This is a constant
+spelling, not a new value type, upload format, meter or protocol capability.
+
+Readable secondary unique collisions with no authored `else CODE` now return
+E_UNIQUE and name the declared key columns, never an internal planner index.
+Authored codes still win. The intrinsic id conflict remains E_CONSTRAINT.
+Hidden collisions retain E_RULE (and hidden write targets retain NOT_FOUND),
+including their deliberately ambiguous public message: a rule denial, unreadable
+key holder or physical authorization cut remain indistinguishable. The wording
+says that a row you cannot read holds this key as one possible cause. Only the
+developer-owned trace may identify the actual private clause. No new hidden
+existence bit is exposed; this preserves LLP 3000 §7 and this RFC §5.
+
+The engine/model/oracles preserve rollback, conflict order, null-key uniqueness,
+if-absent behavior, device prediction and unchanged named refusal precedence.
+Lean's visible secondary conflict code follows E_UNIQUE; explicit row projection
+has the existing field semantics. Generated equivalent implicit/explicit sources,
+Lean examples, simulator and both device stores exercise the projection and
+unique conflict. Native and Lean fixed-seed runs must add no failure signatures.
+
+A development-only check rejects an operation principal argument equal to a
+bare declared persona (alice), naming dev:alice. Static principal column literals
+get advisory N_PERSONA_PRINCIPAL. Production does neither: arbitrary account
+principals remain valid and personas confer no authority. Developer query/test
+output may count observed physical rows filtered by their read rules through
+an opt-in collector, outside the wire envelope and durable receipts. It never
+adds hidden counts to serve, browser responses, sync, the device or output data;
+counts describe encountered rows, not the whole unreadable population.

### 5.2 Composition: helpers with bodies, jobs with preludes

**8. `fn` takes a body.** Today `fn` is one expression and `proc` is a
block that returns nothing, so the 0.1.0 builder wrote the receipt
fan-out three times (`send`, `sendMedia`, `sendPoll`) and the 0.2.6
builder wrote its receipt state as three nested one-line `fn`s. LLP
2000.000 §6 named the split as pricing residue. Proposed: one `fn`,
declared with an expression or with a block ending in `return`, callable
in expression position anywhere; expanded inline as helpers are today
(`bind/program/control.rs`), so a write inside a body is admitted exactly
when the caller may write. **Loop placement also inherits the caller's
enclosing loops:** a helper inside a job's recipient sweep performs ordinary
per-recipient loops; a helper at the job's top level still receives the
automatic-sweep and stable-domain checks. `break` and `continue` remain
lexically scoped to loops inside the helper. A query calling a writing `fn`
is a placement error at the call site, with the site named. `proc` is deleted with the
rewrite `fn` (rules: delete, don't deprecate).

```quarry
fn receiptState(cid: conversations, sender: principal, seq: int):
  unread = 0
  undelivered = 0
  for m in memberships[cid] first 50 by byConversationPrincipal:
    if m.principal = sender or m.joinedSequence >= seq:
      continue
    if m.readSequence < seq:
      unread = unread + 1
    if m.deliveredSequence < seq:
      undelivered = undelivered + 1
  return 'read' if unread = 0 else ('delivered' if undelivered = 0 else 'sent')
```

**2026-09-27 — repeated pure calls (0.4.5 lane QE, calibration #22).**
A null test narrows a repeated `fn` call like a field path of a lexical
snapshot when the expanded helper reads no table, writes nothing and reads
neither `now` nor another changing input (the commit/read clock, a minted id
or connection state). Every argument must be a lexical name, a field path
of a lexical snapshot, a literal, or another such pure call. For example,
`now + windows.ttl(c.disappearing) if windows.ttl(c.disappearing) != null else null`
compiles. A database read used directly as an argument does not qualify;
binding its result once creates a lexical snapshot.

The null fact identifies the helper and ordered arguments, including each
snapshot's lexical identity. It is scoped to the guarded branch, short circuit
or surviving guard and invalidated when any argument root is reassigned or
carried through a changing loop. The binder checks the expanded IR, including
transitive helpers and named shapes, for effects; it never removes a read,
write or clock access to make a call pure. Both calls still execute in source
order under the existing meters. Every other optional call keeps the existing
located `E_QUARRY_TYPE` diagnostic and “bind the optional call once” rewrite.

**2026-10-03 — guarded point reads (lane QE2, calibration #30).**
`require exists t[k]`, `require t[k] != null`, and the present branch of
`if t[k] != null` prove the identical unique-key lookup non-null, including
helper arguments. The binder records stable key identities in the current
lexical state; rebindings, writes (including expanded expression helpers),
branch joins, loop fixed points and job viewer changes invalidate stale facts. Guards containing
writing helpers establish no point fact. Both reads still execute and are
metered. This does not make a table-reading helper pure.

A required reference is a typed id, not an existence constraint. Even when a
parent's read rule is exactly the membership probe just required, a membership
can outlive an absent parent. No parent-existence implication is inferred.
### 5.4 Writes and schema: patching, defaults

**13. `upsert` patches.** Today `upsert t[key] { fields }` replaces the
row; the 0.2.6 builder lost an avatar to it, and every model expects
insert-or-update-these-fields (Postgres `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`,
Convex `patch`). Proposed: when the row exists, the fields are an
`update` patch and unnamed columns keep their values; when it does not,
the fields are an insert and a missing required column refuses `E_INPUT`
naming it. The card's "insert or replace" becomes "insert or patch".

**14. Column defaults.** `at: time default now`, `authorId: principal
default viewer`, `count: int default 0`, `role: enum('member', 'admin')
default 'member'`: an insert may omit a defaulted column; the engine
fills it on the host running the write, as it evaluates an explicit
`at: now` today, so a device's prediction and the server's judgement
agree as they do now. Defaults are literals, `now` and `viewer`; nothing
computed.

**2026-10-03 — total results and live rule references (lane QE2).**
Insert results materialize every ordinary omitted optional column as null and
every omitted default as its evaluated value. Completion runs after authority,
preserves the supplied payload and existing program IR, and meters its result
copy and added fields. Update results keep their
existing authorized reread semantics, including unchanged columns. Private
owned fields keep projection; engine-assigned sequence/receipt fields keep
their existing result and prediction paths. Maintained columns remain a
compile-time E_MAINTAINED_COLUMN_RESULT with a fresh authorized-read rewrite.
Reading a known omitted optional field introduces no prediction dependency.

Each term in insert, update and delete rules admits one live typed-reference hop, including
`.message.conversation` and `messages[.message].conversation`. Named update
rules select their old or next reference; delete selects the pre-delete row.
The target is point-read under current read authority. Absent, expired or
unreadable targets produce an unknown leaf, which cannot authorize even under
negation or equality with null. Each occurrence prepays one rule probe;
reference dependencies join the rule's declared scratch reservation and shared
8,192-row physical authorization allowance. Devices require current covered
authority, including pending chains, and cannot use retained-only witnesses.
The `rule-reference` capability fences older engines.

This live lookup neither replaces nor changes read-through audience capture
and lifetime rules (LLP 3000.014). Deeper hop chains, private/maintained target
fields, ephemeral targets and final after-insert obligations refuse
E_QUARRY_RULE_HOP with a concrete explicit-lookup or read-through rewrite.
Known disallowed relationships do not use E_QUARRY_UNKNOWN.
[QE2 evidence](../snapback4/reports/20261003-qe2-quarry-ergonomics/REPORT.md)
contains baseline failures and server/device verification.

**2026-10-04 — QE2 round 1 allocation and wording correction.**
Sibling depth-one reference terms are legal; every syntactic occurrence prepays
its own probe, including repeated references to the same parent. The depth
restriction applies to chaining through an already followed reference, not to
the number of independent terms; ordinary probe and physical limits still apply.

Result completion prices known default values by their actual clone allocation,
plus field names/slots and the result image, never the column's declared maximum.
An unused compiler-created insert temporary does not demand completion. The
existing exhaustive IR walker conservatively counts variable uses (capped at two)
across all arms, loops and inlined helpers before execution; one use by the
insert itself preserves the move-only discarded path. A discarded `if absent`
result likewise skips completion when its separate receiver has no uses.

//! Expression lowering with branch-owned setup statements.

use super::*;
use snapback4_core::calendar::Civil;

impl Binder<'_> {
    /// Bare tables are domains only at an aggregate/loop consumer; ordinary
    /// names keep their lexical meaning and ordinary pages keep their bounds.
    pub(super) fn aggregate_domain(&self, value: &A) -> Option<ReadExpr> {
        match value {
            A::Read(read) if read.range.is_none() && read.matching.is_none() => Some(read.clone()),
            A::Name { name, site } if self.binding(name).is_none() && self.catalog.tables.contains_key(name) =>
                Some(ReadExpr { cursor_prefix: None, order_keys: Vec::new(), computed: Default::default(), table: name.clone(), keys: Vec::new(), index: Some("byId".into()), range: None, matching: None, filter: None, seeks: Vec::new(), site: site.clone() }),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    // ----- expressions -----

    /// An expression whose value is used (bound, returned, or a final
    /// write): writes yield their row.
    pub(super) fn value_of(&mut self, value: &A, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
        if let A::Write { .. } = value {
            return self.write(value, out, true).map(|opt| opt.expect("a valued write"));
        }
        self.expr(value, out)
    }

    /// Strict compound children run in source order, before setup emitted by
    /// a later child. Lexical values and their fields cannot change here;
    /// leaving those fields in their object also preserves pending provenance.
    pub(super) fn snapshot(&mut self, value: Expr, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Expr {
        if matches!(value, Expr::Literal(_) | Expr::Input(Input::Viewer | Input::Now)) || lexical_value(&value) {
            return value;
        }
        let name = self.temp("value");
        out.push(Stmt::Let { name: name.clone(), value });
        ir::var(&name)
    }

    pub(super) fn sequence_setup<'e>(&mut self, prior: impl Iterator<Item = &'e mut Expr>, setup: setup::Body, out: &mut setup::Body) {
        if !setup.is_empty() {
            for value in prior {
                *value = self.snapshot(std::mem::replace(value, Expr::Literal(Value::Null)), out);
            }
            out.extend(setup);
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn strict_args(&mut self, args: &[A], out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<Vec<(Expr, Ty)>> {
        let mut values = Vec::<(Expr, Ty)>::new();
        let mut failed = None;
        for arg in args {
            let mut setup = setup::Body::default();
            match self.expr(arg, &mut setup) {
                Ok(value) => {
                    self.sequence_setup(values.iter_mut().map(|(e, _)| e), setup, out);
                    values.push(value);
                }
                Err(error) => { self.record_error(error.clone()); failed.get_or_insert(error); }
            }
        }
        match failed { Some(error) => Err(error), None => Ok(values) }
    }

    pub(super) fn expr(&mut self, expr: &A, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
        // Only shape/object/list construction forwards output position. Every
        // operator, call, key, predicate and assertion consumes its operands.
        let prior = self.returned_data;
        self.returned_data &= matches!(expr, A::Array { .. } | A::Object { .. } | A::Shape { .. } | A::ShapeUse { .. } | A::Member { .. } | A::Name { .. } | A::Focal { .. });
        let start = out.len();
        let result = self.expr_inner(expr, out);
        if point_facts::writes(&out[start..]) { self.invalidate_points(); }
        self.returned_data = prior;
        // Even a builtin's ordinary type refusal should explain why a whole
        // maintained value cannot be consumed. Successful calls are checked by
        // the shared IR allowlist; this only improves already-failing calls.
        if result.as_ref().is_err_and(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE") {
            let args: Vec<&A> = match expr { A::Call { args, .. } => args.iter().collect(), A::Binary { left, right, .. } => vec![left, right], _ => vec![] };
            let mut probe = self.clone();
            for arg in args {
                if let Ok((_, ty)) = probe.expr(arg, &mut setup::Body::default()) {
                    self.maintenance_operand(&ty, arg.site())?;
                }
            }
        }
        let result = result?;
        if !self.schema.receipts.is_empty() {
            let site = self.call_chain.iter().find(|(name, _)| self.catalog.documents.iter().flat_map(|d| &d.tables).filter_map(|t| t.receipts.as_ref()).any(|clause| &clause.operations[0] == name))
                .map(|(_, site)| site).unwrap_or_else(|| expr.site());

/// Dev's cast check, for `test` and a local `run`: with `use personas`
/// declared, a bare name (or `dev:<name>`) outside the cast is refused as dev
/// refuses its header (E_AUTH); a principal id such as `user:…` passes as itself.
pub fn undeclared_persona(name: &str, declared: &[String]) -> Option<String> {
    if declared.is_empty() { return None; }
    let bare = match name.split_once(':') { None => name, Some(("dev", bare)) => bare, Some(_) => return None };
    (!declared.iter().any(|p| p == bare)).then(|| format!(
        "persona {bare} is not declared; `use personas {}` is this project's cast, and dev refuses {bare} with E_AUTH (401). Add {bare} to it, or use a declared persona (an outsider is a declared persona with no rows)",
        declared.join(", ")))
}

/// The persona a case without `as` runs as: alice when she is in the cast (or
/// there is none), else the first declared persona.
pub fn default_persona(declared: &[String]) -> &str {
    if declared.is_empty() || declared.iter().any(|p| p == "alice") { "alice" } else { &declared[0] }
}

/// One case as `test`'s query sweep reads it: which query, as whom, with
/// which arguments (`None` when they name a saved answer, which only the case
/// run has), expecting what.
pub struct Explicit { pub at: String, pub op: String, pub principal: String, pub args: Option<Json>, pub expect: Option<String> }

/// The cases file read leniently, before the sweep: a line that does not
/// parse is left to [`run`], which refuses it with its line number.
// @ref LLP 3000.036#15.2 — wave 7: the sweep runs a persona's own case arguments and labels a refusal its case expects.
pub fn explicit(fixture: &str, declared: &[String]) -> Vec<Explicit> {
    let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(Path::new(fixture).join(FILE)) else { return Vec::new() };
    fn saved(value: &Json) -> bool {
        match value { Json::String(text) => text.starts_with('$') && text.len() > 1, Json::Array(items) => items.iter().any(saved), Json::Object(fields) => fields.values().any(saved), _ => false }
    }
    text.lines().enumerate().filter_map(|(index, line)| {
        let line = line.trim();
        if line.is_empty() || line.starts_with("//") { return None; }
        let case: Json = serde_json::from_str(line).ok()?;
        let op = case.get("op")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
        let persona = case.get("as").and_then(Json::as_str).unwrap_or_else(|| default_persona(declared));
        let principal = if persona.contains(':') { persona.to_owned() } else { persona_principal(persona) };
        let args = Some(case.get("args").cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| json!({}))).filter(|args| args.is_object() && !saved(args));
        Some(Explicit { at: format!("{FILE}:{}", index + 1), op, principal, args, expect: case.get("expect").and_then(Json::as_str).map(str::to_owned) })
    }).collect()
}

    /// Whether a value of `self` may be stored where `expected` is declared.
    pub fn assignable_to(&self, expected: &Ty) -> bool {
        if self == expected {
            return true;
        }
        match (self, expected) {
            (Ty::Null, Ty::Optional(_)) => true,
            (Ty::Optional(inner), Ty::Optional(target)) => inner.assignable_to(target),
            (value, Ty::Optional(target)) => value.assignable_to(target),
            (Ty::Text(a), Ty::Text(b)) => a <= b,
            // @ref LLP 3000.007#20 — enum widening is static and total: every variant fits the text bound and character domain.
            (Ty::Enum(variants), Ty::Text(max)) => variants.iter().all(|v| v.chars().count() <= *max as usize && snapback4_core::engine::validate::disallowed_text_control(v).is_none()),
            // A text literal in an enum position is a variant; the binder
            // checks membership where it knows the literal.
            (Ty::Text(_), Ty::Enum(_)) => true,
            (Ty::Id, Ty::Ref(_)) | (Ty::Ref(_), Ty::Id) | (Ty::Id, Ty::Principal) | (Ty::Principal, Ty::Id) => true,
            (Ty::Ref(a), Ty::Ref(b)) => a == b,
            (Ty::Int, Ty::Time) | (Ty::Time, Ty::Int) => true,
            (Ty::Int, Ty::Decimal(_)) | (Ty::Int, Ty::Money(..)) => true,
            (a, b) if a.sequence().is_some() && b.sequence().is_some() => {
                let (a, am) = a.sequence().unwrap();
                let (b, bm) = b.sequence().unwrap();
                a.assignable_to(&b) && am <= bm
            },
            (Ty::Object(a) | Ty::RowShape(a) | Ty::RowObject(a), Ty::Object(b) | Ty::RowShape(b) | Ty::RowObject(b)) => a.len() == b.len() && a.iter().all(|(name, ty)| b.get(name).is_some_and(|target| ty.assignable_to(target))),
            (Ty::Enum(a), Ty::Enum(b)) => a.iter().all(|v| b.contains(v)),
            (Ty::Unknown, _) | (_, Ty::Unknown) | (_, Ty::Json) => true,
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    /// A heap-bound allocation can be written; the row validator checks its
    /// actual length. It cannot claim a smaller bound inside an inline helper.
    pub(crate) fn writable_to(&self, expected: &Ty) -> bool {
        match (self, expected) {
            (Ty::Optional(a), Ty::Optional(b)) => a.writable_to(b),
            (a, Ty::Optional(b)) => a.writable_to(b) || *a == Ty::Null,
            (Ty::Text(u32::MAX), Ty::Text(_)) => true,
            (Ty::List(a, am), Ty::List(b, bm)) => a.writable_to(b) && (*am == u32::MAX || am <= bm),
            _ => self.assignable_to(expected),
        }
    }

    /// Whether two values may meet in `=`, `!=` or a key position.
    pub fn comparable(&self, other: &Ty) -> bool {
        let a = self.required();
        let b = other.required();
        a == b || a.assignable_to(&b) || b.assignable_to(&a) || a == Ty::Null || b == Ty::Null
    }

    /// The type both branches can share. Row-kind conflicts are errors at
    /// their first join, including inside objects and collections.
    pub fn join(&self, other: &Ty) -> Result<Ty, JoinError> {
        self.join_inner(other, false)
    }

    /// Nonempty list items must never erase a conflict into Unknown: a later
    /// item could otherwise recover a type the earlier values do not have.
    // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.1 — literals and concatenation share sound item joins.
    pub(crate) fn join_item(&self, other: &Ty) -> Result<Ty, JoinError> {
        self.join_inner(other, true)
    }

    fn join_inner(&self, other: &Ty, strict: bool) -> Result<Ty, JoinError> {
        if self == other { return Ok(self.clone()); }
        // Absence adds nullability; it supplies no competing wildcard kind.
        if *self == Ty::Null { return Ok(other.clone().optional()); }
        if *other == Ty::Null { return Ok(self.clone().optional()); }

                terminal: false, no_candidate: true, site: site.into(), generation: self.context.generation,
            });
        }
    }
    pub(super) fn refusing_clause(&self, table: &str, clause: &str) {
        self.refusing_phase(table, clause, clause);
    }
    pub(super) fn filtered_clause(&self, table: &str, clause: &str) {
        self.filtered_phase(table, clause, clause);
    }
    pub(super) fn filtered_phase(&self, table: &str, clause: &str, phase: &str) {
        self.record_clause(table, clause, phase, false);
    }
    pub(super) fn refusing_phase(&self, table: &str, clause: &str, phase: &str) {
        self.record_clause(table, clause, phase, true);
    }
    fn record_clause(&self, table: &str, clause: &str, phase: &str, terminal: bool) {
        #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
        if let Some(trace) = &self.context.refusal_trace {
            *trace.0.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) = Some(RefusingClause {
                table: table.into(), viewer: self.context.viewer.clone(), clause: clause.into(), phase: phase.into(), terminal, no_candidate: false, site: self.statement_site.clone(), generation: self.context.generation,
            });
        }
        #[cfg(not(feature = "sqlite"))]
        let _ = (table, clause, phase, terminal);
    }
    pub(super) fn trace_rule_result(&self, result: &Result<bool, RuntimeError>, table: &str, effect: Effect) {
        #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
        if self.context.refusal_trace.is_some() {
            let phase = format!("{effect} rule");
            if matches!(result, Ok(false)) { self.record_clause(table, &phase, &phase, effect != Effect::Read); }
            self.trace_authorization(result, table, effect, &phase);
        }
        #[cfg(not(feature = "sqlite"))]
        let _ = (result, table, effect);
    }
    /// Preserve the phase before enclosing writes remap the public error effect.
    pub(super) fn trace_authorization<T>(&self, result: &Result<T, RuntimeError>, table: &str, effect: Effect, phase: &str) {
        #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
        if self.context.refusal_trace.is_some() && matches!(result, Err(RuntimeError::AuthorizationBudget { .. })) {
            self.refusing_phase(table, &format!("authorization allowance ({effect})"), phase);
        }
        #[cfg(not(feature = "sqlite"))]
        let _ = (result, table, effect, phase);
    }
    pub(super) fn trace_unlocated_budget(&self, table: &str, effect: Effect) {
        #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
        if self.context.refusal_trace.as_ref().is_some_and(|trace| trace.0.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e|e.into_inner()).as_ref().is_none_or(|cause| !cause.clause.starts_with("authorization allowance"))) {
            self.refusing_phase(table, &format!("authorization allowance ({effect})"), "authorization access");
        }
        #[cfg(not(feature = "sqlite"))]
        let _ = (table, effect);
    }
    pub(super) fn rule_refusal(&self, table: &str, effect: Effect, clause: &str) -> RuntimeError {
        self.refusing_clause(table, clause);
        RuntimeError::Rule { table: table.into(), effect }
    }
}

#[test]
// @ref LLP 3000.023#12 — a retained once handle discloses metadata, never permission to fetch bytes again.
fn assets_once_contract_retains_metadata_and_renders_opened() {
    let text = normalize(&card("assets").unwrap());
    for fact in [
        "`once` is a bytes-once contract.",
        "The handle and metadata (id, type, dimensions, byte size) may remain after viewing.",
        "A visible handle is never permission to show content.",
        "When `useAsset` or a fetch refuses with E_ASSET_VIEWED, render \"Opened\" (or similar):",
    ] {
        assert!(text.contains(fact), "assets card omits {fact}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn every_card_separates_headings_from_prose() {
    for name in KEYWORDS {
        let mut fence = None;
        let mut previous_blank = true;
        for line in card(name).unwrap().lines() {
            let trimmed = line.trim_start();
            if let Some(marker) = fence {
                if trimmed.starts_with(marker) { fence = None; }
            } else if let Some(marker) = ["```", "~~~"].into_iter().find(|m| trimmed.starts_with(m)) {
                fence = Some(marker);
            } else if let Some(at) = line.find("# ") {
                assert!(line[..at].chars().all(|c| c == '#' || c.is_whitespace()), "{name}: heading glued to prose: {line}");
                assert!(previous_blank, "{name}: blank line missing before heading: {line}");
            }
            previous_blank = trimmed.is_empty();
        }
    }
}

use snapback4_core::{Context, Engine, Value, WriteState};
use snapback4_lang::{Bound, compile};

fn checked(source: &str) -> Bound {
    let b = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
    assert!(b.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
    b
}
fn engine(b: Bound) -> Engine {
    Engine::memory(b.schema, b.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap()
}
fn context(args: &[(&str, Value)]) -> Context {
    Context::new("alice", args.iter().map(|(k,v)| (k.to_string(), v.clone())).collect()).at(100)
}
const ROWS: &str = "table messages:\n  photo: image <=1000 ?\n  edited: bool default false\n  at: time default now\n  public\n  insert <- allow\n  update <- allow\n  sync public\n";

#[test]
fn insert_result_is_total_and_predictable() {
    let b = checked(&format!("{ROWS}mutation send():\n  m = insert messages {{}}\n  return {{ photo: m.photo, edited: m.edited, at: m.at }}\n"));
    assert_eq!(b.schema.operations["send"].predicts.as_deref(), Some("eligible"));
    let mut e = engine(b);
    let result = e.mutate("send", Some("send"), context(&[]).with_ids(["message".into()])).unwrap();
    let WriteState::Sent { result, .. } = result.state else { panic!("{result:?}") };
    assert_eq!(result.field("photo"), Ok(&Value::Null));
    assert_eq!(result.field("edited"), Ok(&Value::Bool(false)));
    assert_eq!(result.field("at"), Ok(&Value::Int(100)));
}

fn calibration(reverted: bool, direct_guard: bool) -> Bound {
    let mut source = include_str!("fixtures/qe2/cal30/schema.q").to_string();
    if reverted {
        source = source.replace(".disappearing ?? 'off'", ".disappearing");
        source = source.replace("preview: slice(text, 0, 80)", "preview: 'Photo' if m.photo != null else slice(text, 0, 80)");
        source = source.replace("  read through .message\n  insert <- .principal = viewer\n  update <- .principal = viewer", "  read through .message\n  insert <- .principal = viewer and exists members[.message.conversation, viewer]\n  update <- .principal = viewer and exists members[.message.conversation, viewer]");
    }
    if direct_guard {
        source = source.replace("  ttl = config.disappearingTtl(", "  require exists conversations[conversation] else NOT_FOUND\n  ttl = config.disappearingTtl(");
    }
    compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source), ("config.q".into(), include_str!("fixtures/qe2/cal30/config.q").into()), ("schedule.q".into(), include_str!("fixtures/qe2/cal30/schedule.q").into())])
}
#[test]
fn calibration_original_compiles() {
    let b = calibration(false, false);
    assert!(b.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
}
#[test]
fn calibration_reverted_with_explicit_parent_guard_compiles() {
    let b = calibration(true, true);
    assert!(b.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
}
#[test]
fn calibration_membership_alone_gets_exact_parent_rewrite() {
    let b = calibration(true, false);
    assert_eq!(b.diagnostics.len(), 3, "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
    for d in b.diagnostics {
        assert_eq!(d.code, "E_QUARRY_TYPE");
        assert!(d.rewrite.contains("require exists conversations[conversation] else NOT_FOUND"), "{d:?}");
    }
}

                }

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Context {

    pub(crate) refusal_trace: Option<refusal_trace::RefusalTrace>,

    pub(crate) search_retained_candidates: Vec<(String, i64, bool)>,

    pub now: Option<i64>,

    pub(crate) row_provenance: bool,
    /// Digest only: the core resolves it in the admission transaction.
    pub(crate) session_digest: Option<String>,
    /// Original HTTP arguments, before typed decoding or default insertion.
    pub wire_args: Option<serde_json::Value>,
    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
    pub delivery_fingerprint: Option<String>,
    pub(crate) generation: u64,
    /// Ids the caller minted for this run, consumed in order by `new`.
    pub new_ids: VecDeque<String>,
    entropy: u64,
    /// Every id consumed by this execution, including newly minted ids.
    pub(crate) minted_ids: Vec<String>,
    /// The server's live registry behind `connected[p]`, when there is one.
    pub presence: Option<std::sync::Arc<dyn Presence>>,
}

A `search body, caption` line declares searchable columns; `matching q`
chooses a words index for the predicate and order (`guide search`).
A unique key can group time without adding a stored column:

```quarry
table checkins:
  principal: principal
  at: time
  unique principal, day(at) else ALREADY_CHECKED_IN 'One check-in per day.'
  read <- .principal = viewer
  insert <- .principal = viewer
mutation checkin():
  return insert checkins { principal: viewer, at: now }
```

`day`, `hour` and `bucket` use floor ordinals from the UTC epoch. An optional
offset anchors the boundary; `day(at, 8h)` starts at 08:00 UTC. These are index
keys, absent from row shapes, rules and writable columns. Changing a period
or offset rebuilds the index. A sweep may order by a computed key only when
its underlying columns are immutable.

/// One further arm of a union audience. Its legacy window field is refused at admission.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SyncArm {
    pub audience: Audience,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub horizon: Option<Horizon>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Audience {
    /// Every principal holds the same partition.
    Public,
    /// The principal named by this row's column.
    Column(String),
    /// Every principal with a row in `table` whose `prefix` columns equal this
    /// row's `prefix` columns, read from the target's `principal` column.
    Target { table: String, prefix: Vec<String>, principal: String },
}

/// `last N by index`: a device holds at most N rows per group, where the group
/// is the audience prefix, in the index's descending order.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Horizon {
    pub last: u32,
    pub by: String,
}

impl Audience {
    /// The content columns that name this audience's group: none for the
    /// public, the column for a column audience, the prefix for a target.
    pub fn columns(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        match self {
            Audience::Public => Vec::new(),
            Audience::Column(column) => vec![column.clone()],
            Audience::Target { prefix, .. } => prefix.clone(),
        }
    }

    /// `.owner` or `members[.team] by .principal`, as one arm of a `sync to`
    /// line: the recipient is named, so the line binds when the target has
        (None, None) => "int".into(),
    }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.040#13-representation — an unwritten end is the i53 limit itself, so the
// variant stays as small as `Int`'s neighbours (no Option) and the bytes omit it.
pub fn int_floor() -> i64 { -crate::value::I53_MAX }
pub fn int_ceiling() -> i64 { crate::value::I53_MAX }
pub fn is_int_floor(min: &i64) -> bool { *min <= int_floor() }
pub fn is_int_ceiling(max: &i64) -> bool { *max >= int_ceiling() }
/// An int range some i53 value satisfies, with both ends inside i53.
pub fn int_range_valid(min: i64, max: i64) -> bool { int_floor() <= min && min <= max && max <= int_ceiling() }
/// A stored end as written: `None` when it is the i53 limit.
pub fn int_bound(end: i64, limit: i64) -> Option<i64> { (end != limit).then_some(end) }

/// Whether `value` lies inside an inclusive optional range.
pub fn int_in_range(value: i64, min: Option<i64>, max: Option<i64>) -> bool {
    min.is_none_or(|min| value >= min) && max.is_none_or(|max| value <= max)
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Index {
    pub components: Vec<IndexComponent>,
    pub unique: bool,
}

impl Index {
    pub fn of(columns: &[&str], unique: bool) -> Self {
        Self { components: columns.iter().map(|c| IndexComponent::Column((*c).to_owned())).collect(), unique }
    }

    /// Ordered key names: columns and time-function names. A `words(..)`
    /// component contributes nothing here; `word_component` names it.
    /// Use `IndexComponent::column` for actual row fields (such as rule pins).
    pub fn columns(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        self.components.iter().filter_map(|c| c.key_name().cloned()).collect()
    }

    pub fn is_plain(&self) -> bool {
        self.components.iter().all(|c| matches!(c, IndexComponent::Column(_)))
    }

    pub fn uses_column(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.components.iter().any(|component| match component {
            IndexComponent::Column(column) => column == name,
            IndexComponent::Calendar(key) => key.column == name,
            IndexComponent::WordPrefixes { fields, .. } => fields.iter().any(|field| field == name),
            IndexComponent::Contribution(maintain) => maintain.dependencies().contains(name),
        })
    }

    /// The `words(..)` component, if any: its position among the
    /// components and the text columns it tokenizes.
    pub fn word_component(&self) -> Option<(usize, &[String])> {
        self.components.iter().enumerate().find_map(|(position, component)| match component {
            IndexComponent::WordPrefixes { fields, .. } => Some((position, fields.as_slice())),
            IndexComponent::Column(_) | IndexComponent::Calendar(_) | IndexComponent::Contribution(_) => None,
        })
    }

    /// The columns after the first `components` components: a cursor's
    /// suffix, and the order a page continues in. Counted in components,
    /// so a scan whose prefix ends with a word skips the word too.
    pub fn suffix_after(&self, components: usize) -> Vec<String> {
        self.components.iter().skip(components).filter_map(|c| c.key_name().cloned()).collect()
    }

/// Bind one table. A refused line becomes a diagnostic and a `deny` (or an
/// absent sync), so one mistake does not cascade into every reader.
fn bind_table(catalog: &Catalog, info: &TableInfo, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) -> Table {
    let decl = &info.decl;
    let mut columns = BTreeMap::new();
    columns.insert("id".to_owned(), core::ColumnType::Id);
    for column in &decl.columns {
        if let TypeKind::Ref { table } = &column.type_.kind
            && !catalog.tables.contains_key(table)
        {
            diagnostics.push(type_error(&column.site, format!("column {}.{} references unknown table {table}", decl.name, column.name), name_rewrite(table, catalog.tables.keys().map(String::as_str), Some("declare the table, or use id for an opaque identity"))));
        }
        columns.insert(column.name.clone(), scalar_to_column(&column.type_));
    }
    let mut recorded = BTreeMap::new();
    for (path, kind) in &info.recorded {
        let (reference, column) = path.split_once('.').expect("admitted path");
        let TypeKind::Ref { table } = &info.columns[reference].kind else { unreachable!("admitted reference") };
        recorded.insert(path.clone(), core::RecordedField { reference: reference.into(), table: table.clone(), column: column.into() });
        columns.insert(path.clone(), scalar_to_column(kind));
    }
    columns.extend(info.captures.iter().map(|(name, ty)| (name.clone(), scalar_to_column(ty))));
    let mut indexes = BTreeMap::new();
    let mut constraints = Vec::new();
    for index in &info.indexes {
        let mut bound = core::Index::of(&index.columns.iter().map(String::as_str).collect::<Vec<_>>(), index.unique);
        for (position, column) in index.columns.iter().enumerate() {

Round 1 limits the categorical note to a self-table witness whose selected

Round 2 also accepts a residual equality on that exact parent column and term,

can find a witness in another parent group and admit its first insertion.
Unproved forms receive no categorical note. The rewrite names the declared
sequence column and its parent; it does not invent a message table or ordinal

A provably fresh counter contains no hidden history, so allocating its first
ordinal would disclose nothing. Neither `created parent` nor an empty live
child group proves that fact in the current model. An ordinary reference
(including a sequence parent) is not a lifetime-enforcing foreign key. The
counter is shared across participating tables, survives deleted children and
parent identities, and can have history before this parent insertion. Even
an empty physical group may therefore reveal past allocations. Testing the
hidden counter for zero and allowing only that case would itself be a probe.
This lane does not add such an exception or reset a counter. Preserve the
membership audience with the guide's manual parent field, initialized on the
new parent and updated atomically by every sender; alternatively an explicitly
owner-only membership model may use its own read authority. That alternative
changes the roster audience and is not an automatic repair.

The exact refusing clause is developer evidence, separate from `Refusal`.
A host must opt in to a native-only, per-execution in-memory collector. The
collector records schema clause, table, execution site and generation, never
arguments, row images, row keys, credentials or hidden counts. It does not
perform reads, reevaluate rules, change admission, consume/refund meters, or
change receipt serialization. Authorization-budget exhaustion records that
cause, not a guessed false rule. The recorded phase is the authorization actually
executing: capture exhaustion maps to the child's `read through` declaration,
not its unevaluated insert rule. Query readers retain their source map together
with the checked-out engine generation across adoption.

Only `snapback4 dev` opts in. After releasing the engine lock and sending the
response, the host hands each response record to a bounded nonblocking writer queue.
The shared JSON response layer covers every refusal envelope, including asset
authorization refusals (HTTP 404, E_ASSET_UNKNOWN), receipt replays and paths
with no collector. Every record carries operation, code, an instance-scoped
request ID or job ID, wall-clock Unix time in milliseconds, and a shared
sequence. Without an evaluated cause it says `cause not instrumented`; it
never leaves a previous request's cause standing for this refusal. A filtered
read cannot supply the cause of a later terminal refusal in the same request.

/// `check --emit-lean <file.q>`: one file, checked, as the Lean model's
/// schema, helpers and programs (`snapback4_lang::emit::lean`).
// @ref LLP 3000.035#52-stage-2-a-small-lean-core — the emitter's command-line face; the harness calls the library directly
fn emit_lean(file: &str) -> i32 {
    let source = match std::fs::read_to_string(file) {
        Ok(source) => source,
        Err(error) => { eprintln!("cannot read {file}: {error}"); return 2; }
    };
    let name = Path::new(file).file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()).unwrap_or(file).to_owned();
    match snapback4_lang::emit::lean::lean(&[(name, source)]) {
        Ok(module) => { println!("{}", serde_json::to_string_pretty(&module.to_json()).unwrap()); 0 }
        Err(snapback4_lang::emit::lean::LeanError::Diagnostics(problems)) => {
            for problem in problems { eprintln!("{problem}"); }
            1
        }
        Err(snapback4_lang::emit::lean::LeanError::Unsupported(u)) => {
            eprintln!("outside the Lean model's fragment: {u}");
            1
        }
    }
}

pub fn check(options: &Options) -> i32 {

        return releases::check_release(options);
    }
